The interplay between the TS and the coupled-channel dynamics produces characteristic structures in the $K \bar{D}^0 D^{*0}$ invariant mass distributions associated with the $X(3872)$ and its isovector partner $W_{c1}$. In particular, the charged-channel contribution exhibits a distinct structure sensitive to the nearby $W_{c1}$ pole. Our results demonstrate that the TS mechanism provides a promising way to probe the otherwise weak manifestation of the $W_{c1}$, offering a complementary experimental strategy for searching for this predicted state at Belle II and LHCb.

hep-ph.title: Connecting Electroweak Fine-Tuning, Tens-of-GeV Dark Matter, and Exotic Higgs Decays in the GNMSSM
hep-ph.author: Zhaoxia Heng, Fei Li, Haijing Zhou
hep-ph.abstract: In the general next-to-minimal supersymmetric standard model (GNMSSM), we connect electroweak fine-tuning, a singlino dark matter candidate with mass around tens of GeV, and Exotic Higgs Decays, identifying a natural region characterized by the mass hierarchy $m_{\tilde{S}}<m_{\tilde{B}}<m_{\tilde{H}}$ and $\mu_{\rm tot}\in [200, 500]$ GeV. For fine-tuning measure $\Delta \leq 40$, the branching ratio $\mathrm{Br}(h\to a_sa_s)$ falls in the range 7\%$-$25\%, with the pseudoscalar mass $m_{a_s}$ lying mostly between 10 and 20 GeV. This region splits into two viable scenarios consistent with LZ 2024 direct detection: one where the lightest CP-even Higgs $h_1$ is SM-like ($h_1$ case), and another where the second-lightest $h_2$ is SM-like ($h_2$ case). LHC searches for $h\to a_sa_s \to b\bar{b}\tau^+\tau^-$ exclude 12\% (10\%) of samples with 12 GeV $\leq m_{a_s} \leq$ 15.5 GeV in the $h_1$ ($h_2$) case, while a substantial fraction remains accessible at the HL-LHC in the $h_2$ case. Our analysis unifies naturalness, dark matter, and observable exotic Higgs decays, yielding concrete targets for future experiments.

hep-ph.title: Low-lying doubly charmed strange baryons via QCD sum rules
hep-ph.author: Hui-Min Yang, Hua-Xing Chen, Xuan Luo
hep-ph.abstract: We systematically investigate the masses of the low-lying doubly heavy baryons and their $B^*(3/2^+)\to B(1/2^+)\gamma$ radiative transitions within QCD sum rules and light-cone sum rules (LCSR). By constructing mixed interpolating currents, we obtain $M_{\Xi_{cc}}=3.62^{+0.14}_{-0.15}$ GeV, $M_{\Xi_{cc}^*}=3.72^{+0.14}_{-0.13}$ GeV, $M_{\Omega_{cc}}=3.72^{+0.13}_{-0.15}$ GeV, and $M_{\Omega_{cc}^*}=3.82^{+0.13}_{-0.15}$ GeV, together with their doubly bottom partners around $10.27$--$10.34$ GeV. The extracted masses are compatible with the observed $\Xi_{cc}$ and $\Omega_{cc}$ states and predict hyperfine splittings of about $101^{+27}_{-11}$ MeV and $99^{+11}_{-12}$ MeV for the $\Xi_{cc}$ and $\Omega_{cc}$ systems, respectively. Using these inputs, we derive the LCSR for the electromagnetic form factors and obtain radiative widths $\Gamma(\Xi_{cc}^{*++}\to\Xi_{cc}^{++}\gamma)=5.25^{+8.57}_{-3.62}$ keV, $\Gamma(\Xi_{cc}^{*+}\to\Xi_{cc}^{+}\gamma)=0.31^{+0.84}_{-0.25}$ keV, and $\Gamma(\Omega_{cc}^{*+}\to\Omega_{cc}^{+}\gamma)=0.41^{+0.67}_{-0.30}$ keV, while the corresponding doubly bottom widths are at the $0.002$--$0.01$ keV level. We find that the magnetic-dipole contribution dominates, whereas the electric-quadrupole form factor is numerically small. The light- and heavy-quark photon-emission terms can interfere or enhance significantly, and the heavy-quark contribution cannot be neglected in radiative transitions. These results provide useful theoretical guidance for future searches for spin-$3/2$ doubly heavy baryons through radiative decay modes at LHCb, Belle II, and other experimental facilities.

hep-ph.title: Hamiltonian Truncation Framework for Gauge Theories on the Interval
hep-ph.author: Rachel Houtz, James Ingoldby
hep-ph.abstract: In this work, we investigate gauge theories in two dimensions nonperturbatively using the Hamiltonian truncation approach. Working on a spatial interval and adopting the axial gauge, we remove all gauge field degrees of freedom and express the interacting Hamiltonian in the eigenbasis of the free Dirac theory, truncated at a finite energy. As a benchmark we analyse the Schwinger model, where our numerical spectra agree closely with the exact results from bosonization across a wide range of couplings, validating the construction of the Hamiltonian. We then generalize the formulation to nonabelian gauge groups and apply it to SU(3) gauge theory with a single massless Dirac fermion. These results demonstrate that gauge theories can be explored nonperturbatively using a truncated Hamiltonian that generates evolutions in ordinary time, offering a complementary alternative to lattice field theory.

hep-ph.title: BPS vortex from nonpolynomial scalar QED in a $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^1$-Maxwell theory
hep-ph.author: F. C. E. Lima
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate a generalized gauged $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^1$-Maxwell theory in which the electromagnetic sector acquires a field-dependent magnetic permeability generated dynamically through fermionic vacuum polarization. We couple a Dirac fermion with an effective mass to a gauged $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^1$ sigma model whose target space carries the Fubini-Study metric. Integrating out the Dirac fermion at one loop induces a logarithmic correction to the Maxwell kinetic term. This dependence is retained in the planar effective theory after dimensional reduction. Within this framework, one builds a generalized $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^1$-Maxwell model by admitting Bogomol'nyi-Prasad-Sommerfield (BPS) configurations. Taking this into account, we solved the self-dual equations that describe vortex-like solutions with quantized magnetic flux.

hep-ph.title: Probing String-Theory-Inspired Topologies of the Early Universe through CMB Temperature and Polarization Anisotropies
hep-ph.author: Nick E. Mavromatos, Miguel-Angel Sanchis-Lozano
hep-ph.abstract: TeV string-mass-scale strings have been excluded experimentally at colliders, as their effects have not been observed at the Large Hadron Collider (CERN). On the other hand, higher-scale string theory, with mass scales typically close to the Planck scale, is often regarded as experimentally inaccessible due to the enormous energies required for direct tests, and far beyond the reach of present or foreseeable particle accelerators. Nevertheless, the early Universe may provide an indirect observational window for high-string scale through imprints left on the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB). In this work, building on previous studies, we reexamine temperature and polarization angular correlations as probes of the geometry and topology of the pre-inflationary Universe. We focus in particular on two-point correlation functions at large angular scales, where signatures of nontrivial spatial topology may survive as relics of primordial physics. We investigate the observational consequences of toroidal compactification and analyze their impact on the primordial power spectrum of the CMB provided by the Planck satellite. Within the current experimental and theoretical uncertainties, we identify a possible indication closely related to spatial-parity breaking, consistent with the presence of six spatial extra dimensions in the early Universe, compactified at the GUT epoch before the start of inflation. Finally, we extend our framework to B-mode polarization, highlighting its potential as a sensitive probe in forthcoming ground-based and space-borne experiments with unprecedented precision.

hep-ph.title: Quantum Field Approach to Relativistic Turbulence
hep-ph.author: Esteban Calzetta
hep-ph.abstract: The goal of this work is to apply quantum field theory methods to a typical relativistic hydrodynamic model. We shall take as representative model an Israel-Stewart framework, where the energy-momentum conservation laws for a conformal invariant fluid are supplemented by a Cattaneo-Maxwell equation for its viscous energy-momentum tensor. In these models the viscous energy-momentum tensor relaxes to its Landau-Lifshitz value on a finite time scale. We assume the parameters of the model depend on the speed of light $c$ in such a way that as $c\to\infty$ the fluid becomes an incompressible fluid obeying the Navier-Stokes equations. We show that because the relativistic model must be hyperbolic, each mode behaves as an overdamped oscillator with two decay constants, one of which diverges as $c\to\infty$. Thus for finite $c$ there are two basic patterns, one which contains only slowly decaying modes, and reproduces Kolmogorov turbulence when $c\to\infty$, and another made of fast decaying modes only. Each flow pattern is associated to definite relations among the velocity and viscous energy tensor correlators.

hep-ph.title: Short Gravitational-Wave Transients as Probes of Cosmic Domain Walls
hep-ph.author: Tore Boybeyi, Doga Veske, David Maibach
hep-ph.abstract: GW190521 and GW231123 have been reported as short-duration gravitational-wave transients consistent with very massive binary black hole (BBH) coalescences whose inferred parameters, i.e., exceptionally high total masses and spin magnitudes, challenge standard isolated binary stellar evolution. We test a topological dark matter (TDM) interpretation invoking cosmic domain walls by fitting a physically motivated domain wall template to the LIGO Hanford and Livingston strain data. The BBH hypothesis is individually favored, with $\log_{10}\mathcal{B}_{\rm BBH/TDM}=12.2$ and $11.3$ for GW231123 and GW190521, respectively. However, these values are lower than those typically recovered from matched maximum a posteriori BBH waveforms injected into nearby noise segments. We further perform, for the first time, a joint fit in which domain wall signals from a single underlying scalar field are constrained simultaneously by both events. Although not favored over BBH signals, we find the two events are consistent with a common scalar field, with shared TDM parameters agreeing across independent noise realizations and sky locations. We further find that injected TDM transients are systematically recovered under the BBH hypothesis with large spin parameters, revealing a morphological degeneracy that could mask genuine domain wall signals. This analysis demonstrates that multi-event parameter consistency tests provide a new discriminant for domain wall dark matter searches in upcoming observing runs.

hep-ph.title: Fermi-eROSITA cross-correlations suggest annihilation lines of $\sim70$ GeV WIMPs
hep-ph.author: Uri Keshet
hep-ph.abstract: The deep potential wells of galaxy clusters provide some of the strongest constraints on the velocity-dependent ($p$-wave) annihilation of weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) dark matter. Cross-correlating high-latitude Fermi-LAT 16.3-year data with the western Galactic hemisphere eROSITA map facilitates high-sensitivity tests. A blind composite matched-filter scan of the cross-correlated spectrum for the $\chi\chi\to\gamma\gamma$, $\gamma Z$, and $\gamma h$ annihilation-line triad of a single WIMP $\chi$ finds $m_\chi c^2\simeq71.9$ and $67.5$ GeV (observer-frame) triads, each with a local $Z$-score $\sim3$ and a (henceforth global) $1.7$-$2.1\sigma$ (trial-corrected), insensitive to details of detrending, sky masks, and filters. The leading nonad (equidistant three triads) corresponds to $66.4$ and $71.9$ GeV cross-annihilating WIMPs ($2.5\sigma$). The leading $\sim72$ GeV triad coincides with the mass implied by interpreting the reported $\sim43.2$ GeV $\gamma$-ray line in three nearby clusters as its $\gamma Z$ channel. At this externally fixed mass, the triad reaches $3.0\sigma$ alone, and $5.1\sigma$ when combined with the reported line ($3.8\sigma$ under alternative assumptions; similar values for the nonad). This triad, absent from the ambient (X-ray-uncorrelated) spectrum, presents in different Galactic sectors, strengthens under cosmological (positive) but not negative redshift broadening $\Delta z$, and peaks at $\Delta z\simeq 0.05$, consistent with galaxy clusters; its two non-$43$ GeV channels reach $2.4\sigma$ by themselves. Measured (not loss-corrected) intrinsic cross sections are a few $10^{-19}$ cm$^3$ s$^{-1}$ for WIMPs tracing the X-ray gas.

hep-ph.title: The Status of Single Scalar Field Dark Energy
hep-ph.author: Carlos García-García, Pedro G. Ferreira, William J. Wolf
hep-ph.abstract: We present an assessment of the current observational status of single scalar field models of dark energy. Motivated by recent cosmological measurements -- including baryon acoustic oscillations, Type Ia supernovae, and CMB data -- we examine whether a dynamical scalar field offers a viable explanation for the accelerated expansion of the Universe. Working within an effective field theory (EFT) framework, we argue that cosmological observations are fundamentally limited and can at most constrain a small number of parameters that govern scalar field dynamics. We show that quintessence remains only marginally distinguishable from a cosmological constant, $\Lambda$, and that more general EFT extensions exhibit modest statistical preference, though such evidence is sensitive to data set selection and prior assumptions. These extended models generically predict fifth forces and modifications to the growth of structure, raising challenges from astrophysical constraints. We compare their predictions with current growth rate measurements, Integrated Sachs-Wolfe (ISW) effect and Solar System constraints. We emphasize that viable screening mechanisms remain theoretically non-trivial and observationally testable. On the other hand, we find that current ISW and growth data remain largely in agreement. Looking ahead to Stage IV surveys we forecast improvements in constraints on the dark energy behaviour; although there will be some tightening of bounds, we argue that the problem of underdetermination will persist. We conclude that while single scalar field dark energy remains a natural and flexible framework, its ultimate viability will hinge on improved low-redshift growth measurements and a clearer understanding of gravitational screening.

hep-ph.title: Symmetry-based resolution of pseudogauge ambiguities in local equilibrium
hep-ph.author: Carlos Hoyos
hep-ph.abstract: The total angular momentum current can be decomposed into orbital and spin contributions in different ways, known as pseudogauges. This freedom leads to ambiguities in the definition of local-equilibrium density operators, which in turn affect estimates of spin polarization in heavy-ion collisions. In this work, the pseudogauge ambiguity, together with other ambiguities associated with improvements of conserved currents, is reformulated in terms of spurious symmetries corresponding to conserved currents with vanishing total charge. A prescription for the unambiguous definition of a local-equilibrium density operator, defined as deviating from global equilibrium only by small gradients, is introduced using the currents associated with genuine symmetries. The resulting density operator is invariant under transformations that add improvement terms to local currents, including the energy-momentum tensor.

hep-ph.title: First Lattice Calculation of Structure-Dependent Radiative Corrections to Lepton-Flavor-Universality Ratios in Leptonic Decays
hep-ph.author: Peter Boyle, Norman H. Christ, Xu Feng, Taku Izubuchi, Luchang Jin, Christopher T. Sachrajda, Xin-Yu Tuo
hep-ph.abstract: The ratio of electronic to muonic leptonic decay widths, $R_{e/\mu}$, for the light mesons $\pi$ and $K$, provides a clean test of lepton flavor universality (LFU) and a sensitive probe of physics beyond the Standard Model. Its Standard-Model prediction is exceptionally precise, with the leading uncertainty associated with the structure-dependent (SD) radiative correction of $O(0.1\%)$. As experiments such as PIONEER and NA62 aim for unprecedented precision, this SD correction has become an essential ingredient in precision experiment--theory comparisons. We present the first lattice QCD$+$QED calculation of this SD correction at the physical pion mass and in the continuum limit. We employ the infinite-volume reconstruction (IVR) method with Coulomb-gauge photons, significantly reducing both statistical errors and finite-volume effects. We obtain the Standard-Model predictions, $R_{e/\mu}=1.23516(10)\times10^{-4}$ for $\pi$ and $R_{e/\mu}=2.47661(31)\times10^{-5}$ for $K$. Our results reduce the hadronic uncertainty in $R_{e/\mu}$, provide the most precise Standard-Model predictions to date, and establish first-principles benchmarks for future high-precision tests of LFU.

hep-ph.title: Combinatorial Residual Network: a decay-chain-aware classifier without explicit jet assignment
hep-ph.author: John Alison, Patrick Bryant, Alejandro Gomez Espinosa, Christian Guinto-Brody, Aniket Khanal, Chuyuan Liu, Sindhu Murthy, Guanglei Zhao
hep-ph.abstract: Final states with several jets from the decays of heavy particles pose a combinatorial problem: the jets must be assigned, at least implicitly, to their parent particles. The Combinatorial Residual Network (CoReNet) is a classifier that encodes the assumed decay chain in its architecture, building the event representation level by level along the decay hierarchy and combining all jet assignment hypotheses, evaluated with shared weights, with learned weights. The exchange symmetries of the decay are built in, the network size does not depend on the number of hypotheses, and no generator-level jet assignments are used in training. Developed for the $b\bar{b}b\bar{b}$ final state and used in several CMS searches, CoReNet with 1508 parameters performs well above kinematic baselines on fast-simulated Higgs boson pair production against QCD multijet events and trains in minutes on a single GPU, and its hypothesis weights select the truth-matched jet pairing in most signal events in which it is defined. Since only the encoded decay chain is specific to the final state, we test the construction on $HH \to b\bar{b}W^+W^-$ against semileptonic $t\bar{t}$, where encoding the decay chain of the background as well improves the classification at a cost of about $10^{3}$ parameters. In both final states, CoReNet performs comparably to a state-of-the-art transformer-based network more than two orders of magnitude larger. The implementation is publicly available atthis https URL.

hep-ph.title: Quark-mass dependence of two-nucleon scattering
hep-ph.author: Jorge Baeza-Ballesteros, André Baião-Raposo, Davide Laudicina, Malcolm Lazarow, Thomas R. Richardson, Miguel Salg, John Bulava, M.A. Clark, Jeremy R. Green, Andrew Hanlon, Renwick J. Hudspith, Daniel Mohler, Colin Morningstar, Amy Nicholson, Fernando Romero-López, André Walker-Loud, Hartmut Wittig(for the Baryon Scattering Collaboration)
hep-ph.abstract: Understanding how the properties of the visible Universe depend on the parameters of the Standard Model of particle physics requires \emph{ab initio} theoretical computations. To that end, we investigate the quark-mass dependence of low-energy nucleon-nucleon scattering in the deuteron and dineutron channels. We perform lattice-QCD calculations at pion masses $M_\pi\approx 200$ and $280$ MeV and compare their results to phenomenology at the physical point and to a previous calculation at $M_\pi\approx 710$ MeV. Scattering amplitudes, phase shifts, and threshold parameters are determined from finite-volume spectra using quantization conditions that explicitly incorporate long-distance effects from one-pion exchange. We analyze the pion-mass dependence of scattering lengths and effective ranges using chiral effective field theory with Weinberg and Kaplan-Savage-Wise power countings. From this, we estimate the pion-mass derivatives of the inverse scattering lengths and binding momentum, at the physical point. Both power countings indicate that the deuteron unbinds near $M_\pi\approx 220$ MeV.

hep-lat.title: Nonperturbative lattice simulation of the nucleation rate in thermal first-order phase transitions
hep-lat.author: Jing Zhou, Ligong Bian
hep-lat.abstract: We present a nonperturbative lattice study of vacuum decay through bubble nucleation in a three-dimensional real scalar field theory at finite temperature. The vacuum decay rate is computed by combining an expanded-ensemble multicanonical hybrid Monte Carlo approach, which samples the critical bubble configurations, with real-time Langevin dynamics, which follows the subsequent bubble evolution. We extrapolate the nucleation rate to the continuum limit and compare it with the corresponding one-loop perturbative prediction, finding a discrepancy of about \(8\%\).

hep-lat.title: Spatiotemporal K-Shape: Reconstructing inhomogeneous condensate profiles on the lattice
hep-lat.author: Keita Horie, Rin Kagami, Chiho Nonaka
hep-lat.abstract: Spatially modulated chiral condensates can affect the phase structure of dense QCD effective models. Understanding such order requires characterizing its real-space structure as well as detecting a modulation. Spatial two-point correlators retain the ensemble-averaged power spectrum but discard relative Fourier phases, leaving the configuration shapes undetermined in general. We propose the Spatiotemporal K-Shape method to extract representative shapes from lattice Monte Carlo ensembles without assuming a functional form. The method extends K-Shape clustering to periodic lattice fields, aligning configurations modulo translations and, optionally, a global sign or phase before extracting cluster centroids. Comparisons across clusterings assess whether one representative shape suffices. Controlled tests recover distinct profiles with identical correlators and separate mixtures of different shapes. Applied to the $(1+1)$-dimensional Gross-Neveu model with $N_f=8$, the method extracts non-sinusoidal profiles with two sign changes at two chemical potentials and separates multiple shape families at a third, where a single centroid is insufficient. Including the discrete chiral sign symmetry in the alignment can fold domain-length fluctuations into an asymmetric centroid without implying a preferred ensemble asymmetry. The method thus complements correlator diagnostics with representative real-space shapes and information on their diversity. The application to the Gross-Neveu model provides a testing ground for configuration-based studies of inhomogeneous order relevant to the QCD phase diagram.

hep-lat.title: Fate of chiral and $U(1)_A$ symmetries in hot QCD matter under background magnetic fields
hep-lat.author: Dan Zhang, Heng-Tong Ding, José Javier Hernández Hernández
hep-lat.abstract: We summarize our recent lattice QCD study of chiral and singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking in background magnetic fields. The magnetic field explicitly reduces the non-singlet flavor symmetry through the unequal light-quark electric charges. We therefore study two neutral-channel susceptibility differences: $\chi_{\pi^0}-\chi_\sigma$ for chiral symmetry breaking and $\chi_{\pi^0}-\chi_{\delta^0}$ for singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking. The calculation uses fixed-scale $(2+1)$-flavor HISQ ensembles with $m_l=m_s^{\mathrm{phys}}/10$, corresponding to a zero-field pion mass of $M_\pi\simeq220\,\mathrm{MeV}$. Magnetic fields enhance both susceptibility differences at low temperatures. Near the crossover, sufficiently strong fields instead suppress both differences. The suppression sets in at larger magnetic fields and is milder for the singlet-axial susceptibility difference than for the neutral chiral susceptibility difference.

hep-lat.title: Canonical partition function and equation of state in the heavy quark region of finite-density lattice gauge theory
hep-lat.author: Shinji Ejiri, Hideya Hashizume, Masanari Koiida
hep-lat.abstract: We investigate the phase structure and equations of state in lattice gauge theory at finite temperature and finite density, focusing on the canonical partition function obtained by decomposing the grand partition function with respect to particle number. We demonstrate that when quark masses are heavy, the complex phase of the quark determinant, which causes the sign problem, can be controlled by decomposing the grand partition function according to particle number. In this study, we propose an algorithm to calculate the canonical partition function for heavy-quark, high-density effective theory and test it for the first time using one-flavor $SU(2)$ gauge theory, a case where the sign problem arises. When the grand partition function of $SU(2)$ is decomposed into canonical partition functions, the sign problem is serious in odd-particle sectors, while it is mild in even-particle sectors. The odd-particle sectors also expose a fundamental issue: center symmetry makes the canonical partition function of $SU(N_c)$ vanish unless the particle number is an integer multiple of $N_c$. Although appropriate in the confinement phase, this restriction must be treated carefully in the deconfinement phase. We resolve the issue by introducing an infinitesimal external field, calculate the canonical partition functions by Monte Carlo simulation, reconstruct the grand partition function, and determine thermodynamic observables over a wide range of temperature and density. Furthermore, we find that the chemical-potential dependence of the equation of state at low temperatures exhibits behavior characteristic of the hadron resonance gas model, and that no softening of the QCD matter occurs at finite density.

hep-lat.title: Transferable neural-network preconditioners for Wilson--Clover propagator inversions
hep-lat.author: Shiyi Zhong, Yuanyi Zhang, Jian-Hui Zhang, Dian-Jun Zhao
hep-lat.abstract: We investigate two single--layer neural-network architectures for accelerating four-dimensional Wilson--Clover propagator inversions on lattice ensembles in practical use; both transfer directly without retraining. The first is a gauge-covariant parallel transport convolution (PTC) network that directly reduces the number of generalized conjugate residual (GCR) solver iterations. The second is a CNN-like network used together with a multigrid-inspired algorithm. The two approaches can be combined to further reduce GCR iterations. PTC transfers without retraining across lattice volumes, lattice spacings, and pion masses while maintaining comparable acceleration, whereas the CNN-like network transfers directly from small- to large-volume ensembles with strong acceleration. A cost comparison accounting for both basis construction and solves shows that the proposed scheme is more advantageous for large-volume ensembles than for small-volume ones.

hep-lat.title: Global analysis of the $ρ$ resonance in lattice QCD
hep-lat.author: Luka Jevsenak, Luka Leskovec, Stefan Meinel, John Negele, Srijit Paul, Andrew Pochinsky
hep-lat.abstract: We present a lattice-QCD study of the $\rho$ resonance in which we address the quark-mass and lattice-spacing dependence in a novel way using a global analysis of four $N_f=2+1$ ensembles. We parametrize discretization effects in the lattice energy levels and not in the scattering amplitude, which is defined in the continuum. We describe the amplitude using a $K$-matrix parameterization, which contains the light- and strange-quark mass dependence. By varying the parameterizations of quark-mass and lattice-spacing dependence, we examine the sensitivity of the physical-limit $\rho$ pole position to these choices and obtain the result $\sqrt{s}_\rho = 744(11)(7) - i\,69(7)(3)~\text{MeV}$ from a model average.

hep-lat.title: Finite temperature Sp(4) lattice gauge theory with matter fields
hep-lat.author: Chris Allton, Ed Bennett, Luigi Del Debbio, Ryan C. Hill, Deog Ki Hong, Jong-Wan Lee, C.-J. David Lin, Biagio Lucini, Maurizio Piai, Davide Vadacchino, Alexis Verney-Provatas
hep-lat.abstract: We perform the first finite-temperature lattice study of the Sp(4) gauge theory coupled to two Wilson-Dirac fermions transforming in the fundamental representation. Its continuum limit plays an important role in many extensions of the Standard Model for particle physics with composite dynamics. For example, it provides a compelling realisation of the strongly interacting massive particle (SIMP) paradigm for dark matter. If realised in nature, it might lead to a first-order thermal phase transition in the early universe, and produce a detectable relic stochastic background of gravitational waves (GW). Assessing whether future experiments are sensitive to the resulting GW power spectrum requires determining the strength of the transition. We scan the parameter space of this lattice theory with a fine mesh of choices of lattice coupling, for two small values of the temporal extent of the lattice, and several choices of spatial volume and fermion mass. We measure the Polyakov loop and its susceptibility on the ensembles generated, implement reweighting, and perform a finite volume analysis, both to classify the nature of the phase transition, and to estimate the critical coupling. We validate our algorithms and analysis procedures on the better understood Sp(4) Yang-Mills theory, by confirming the presence of a first-order phase transition. Upon coupling the theory to matter fields, in the presence of moderately light fermions, the Polyakov loop shows a clear crossover behaviour and does not detect singularities associated with a phase transition. We also uncover the first evidence of a first-order thermal phase transition in the case of the largest fermion masses available. This finding motivates future, large-scale studies aimed at characterising the transition in the continuum limit, for this and closely related theories with Sp(2N) gauge group.

hep-lat.title: Hadron structure on the 16-cell honeycomb
hep-lat.author: Sandor Katz, Daniel Nogradi
hep-lat.abstract: In previous work we started a program of studying non-perturbative QCD on the 4-dimensional 16-cell honeycomb lattice instead of the usually adopted cubic lattice. It was shown that in several observables much smaller cut-off effects are observed, undoubtedly a result of the larger space-time symmetry of this discretization. In the present work further consequences are worked out, relevant for the lattice determination of hadronic structure functions. The key ingredient is the larger set of irreducible representations of the 16-cell honeycomb symmetry group relative to the cubic lattice, leading to more protection from mixing and thus less power divergences. A second ingredient is that more irreducible representations are available for a hadron at rest, which also leads to computational gain in practice. The analysis is given in full detail for both polarized and unpolarized and both forward and off-forward matrix elements of twist-2 and twist-3 operators. It is shown that a larger set of moments can be determined with continuum-like renormalization and at rest, than on the cubic lattice.

hep-lat.title: Determination of $V_{ud}$ from superallowed $β$ decays using effective field theory
hep-lat.author: Samuel Novario, Graham Chambers-Wall, Vincenzo Cirigliano, Wouter Dekens, Jordy de Vries, Stefano Gandolfi, Martin Hoferichter, Emanuele Mereghetti
hep-lat.abstract: A precision determination of $V_{ud}$ from superallowed $\beta$ decays requires exquisite control over radiative corrections, including nuclear-structure-dependent effects whose evaluation has traditionally relied on nuclear models. To assess the uncertainties inherent in the nuclear matrix elements, an alternative strategy based on effective field theory (EFT) has been established in recent years. Here, we present material progress in this program, in terms of a first EFT calculation of the crucial correction $\bar\delta_\text{NS}$ for 12 superallowed transitions ranging from $^{10}$C $\rightarrow$ $^{10}$B to $^{54}$Co $\rightarrow$ $^{54}$Fe. These main results rely on nuclear ab initio calculations using the coupled cluster method, benchmarked against Quantum Monte Carlo evaluations for light nuclei. The global fit to superallowed decay rates reveals that the precision in $V_{ud}$ is currently limited by short-distance contributions that in the EFT are parameterized as two-nucleon contact interactions, leading to an uncertainty $\delta V_{ud}\simeq 6\times 10^{-4}$. We discuss the consequences for the status of the first-row unitarity test of the CKM matrix as well as a roadmap how to reduce the uncertainty in $V_{ud}$ in the future.

hep-lat.title: Ab initio calculations of ${\barδ_\text{NS}}$ and extraction of ${V_{ud}}$ using effective field theory
hep-lat.author: Samuel Novario, Graham Chambers-Wall, Vincenzo Cirigliano, Wouter Dekens, Jordy de Vries, Stefano Gandolfi, Martin Hoferichter, Emanuele Mereghetti
hep-lat.abstract: Radiative corrections limit the precision of $V_{ud}$ extractions from superallowed $\beta$ decays. In particular, the model dependence in the nuclear matrix elements (NMEs) is difficult to assess without a clear organizing principle, which is provided by effective field theory (EFT). We report substantial progress in this program based on ab initio nuclear calculations using the coupled cluster method. Benchmarking results against Quantum Monte Carlo calculations for light nuclei, we evaluate all two-body NMEs that enter the correction $\bar\delta_\text{NS}$ across 12 superallowed transitions relevant for $V_{ud}$, including an estimate of truncation and Hamiltonian uncertainties. We find that certain three-body NMEs at ${\mathcal O}(\alpha^2)$ play an important role, due to a combination of large numerical prefactors and coherent scaling with $Z^2$. We develop a formalism to estimate such NMEs based on nuclear densities to complete the EFT evaluation of $\bar\delta_\text{NS}$, validating the corresponding two-body NMEs against ab initio calculations. We further identify the corrections in the traditional phase-space factor that are captured by the EFT and remove them consistently, which renders the individual transitions mutually consistent. Profiting from a recent calculation of ${\mathcal O}(\alpha^2 Z)$ ultrasoft photons, we find that the scale uncertainty in the EFT is now negligible, while the remaining uncertainty is dominated by contact terms required to renormalize the magnetic Gamow-Teller NMEs. One combination of low-energy constants can be determined from a global fit to the superallowed data, but the second one proves strongly correlated with $V_{ud}$, necessitating additional input to resolve the nuclear-structure effects. We argue that such short-distance contributions currently imply an uncertainty in $V_{ud}$ at the level of $\delta V_{ud}\simeq 6\times 10^{-4}$.

hep-lat.title: Confinement--Higgs Complementarity Viewed through Relative Quantum Reference Frames
hep-lat.author: Kei-Ichi Kondo
hep-lat.abstract: We formulate confinement--Higgs complementarity in terms of the relative orientation between two independently constructed quantum reference frames (QRFs): one derived from the gauge field and the other from the scalar field. Exact continuum and lattice identities give a relational interpretation of the scalar--color observables used in recent gauge-fixing-free $SU(2)$ simulations. In particular, we provide a QRF interpretation of the additional gauge-invariant nonlocal separation line obtained from the Cho--Duan--Ge (CDG) reduction reported in lattice simulations of the radially fixed fundamental $SU(2)$ gauge--scalar model. We explain why such a candidate nonlocal boundary is compatible with Fradkin--Shenker continuity and Osterwalder--Seiler analyticity for the appropriate class of local gauge-invariant observables. Separately, we show that a Wilson-rooted control observable admits an exact results at zero plaquette coupling and that it does not cause such a nonlocal separation line.

hep-lat.title: Wilsonian renormalization group flow in QED with the Pauli term
hep-lat.author: Sorato Nagao, Hiroshi Suzuki
hep-lat.abstract:
We study the renormalization group (RG) flow of quantum electrodynamics (QED) with a Pauli term, $\kappa_	au\Bar{\psi}\sigma_{\mu
u}F_{\mu
u}\psi$, by using the gradient flow exact renormalization group (GFERG). In the GFERG, the gauge Ward--Takahashi identity takes the conventional form and is exactly preserved, and the gauge coupling flows only through the photon anomalous dimension~$\gamma_A$. In the leading large-$N_f$ approximation, the vacuum polarization induced by the Pauli coupling yields a nontrivial fixed point with~$e_*=0$, $\kappa_*
eq0$, and~$\gamma_A=-1$. This fixed point has three relevant directions, as does one of the fixed points of the asymptotically safe QED proposed by Gies and Ziebell. At finite~$N_f$, however, the $N_f$-independent one-loop effects on the fermion line, in particular the additive mass renormalization proportional to~$\kappa^2$, eliminate this fixed point unless $N_f$ is at least several tens; for~$N_f=1$ there is no fixed point at weak Pauli coupling. Along the full flow for~$N_f=1$, $\kappa_	au$ is irrelevant and is attracted to an induced value~$\kappa_{	ext{ind}}(e_	au)$, which is proportional to~$e_	au^3$ at weak coupling, while $e_	au^2$ is marginally irrelevant as in QED without the Pauli term.

hep-lat.title: On reflection positivity of lattice chiral fermions
hep-lat.author: Zhiyao Lu, Shu-Heng Shao
hep-lat.abstract: We point out that the overlap Weyl fermion, the spacetime lattice realization of a Weyl fermion underlying Lüscher's construction of lattice chiral gauge theories, is not reflection positive in two and four dimensions at finite lattice spacing. Consequently, the standard Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction does not yield a Hilbert space with a self-adjoint Hamiltonian. In two dimensions, we further show that the overlap Weyl fermion cannot be cut open: the lattice action becomes nonlocal in the presence of a boundary, as expected from the gravitational anomaly of the continuum field theory. By contrast, the overlap Dirac fermion is known to be reflection positive. However, its compact axial symmetry is not invariant under the reflection, whereas a reflection-invariant axial symmetry is noncompact, and both are part of an Onsager algebra.

hep-lat.title: HVP contributions to the muon anomalous magnetic moment in spacelike and timelike domains
hep-lat.author: A.V.Nesterenko
hep-lat.abstract: The hadronic vacuum polarization contributions to the muon anomalous magnetic moment $a^{\text{HVP}}_{\mu}$ in spacelike and timelike domains are recapped. The values of $a^{\text{HVP}}_{\mu}$ assessed within dispersively-improved perturbation theory are reported. The obtained results can be employed in the evaluations of $a^{\text{HVP}}_{\mu}$ in the framework of such methods as lattice studies, MUonE project, and others.

hep-lat.title: Doubly strange tetraquark as a $KK^*$ virtual state: quark-model study with harmonic traps
hep-lat.author: Kai-Kai Zhang, Zi-Yang Lin, Yan-Ke Chen, Lu Meng
hep-lat.abstract: We extract hadron--hadron scattering information from quark-level interactions using an artificial harmonic trap and a four-quark basis that includes both meson--meson and compact diquark--antidiquark configurations. Combining the Busch--Englert--Rzażewski--Wilkens formula with the effective range expansion (ERE), we determine phase shifts, scattering lengths, effective ranges, and pole positions from the trapped spectrum. We control uncertainties from basis truncation, finite trap frequencies, truncation of ERE, and quark-model parameters. The extracted $DD^*$ and $BB^*$ binding energies agree with direct calculations, providing benchmarks. For the doubly strange $T_{ss}$ with $I(J^P)=0(1^+)$, we predict a $KK^*$ virtual-state pole about 30--35~MeV below threshold in the stable-$K^*$ approximation. Both the AL1 model and its modified version that better reproduces the measured $T_{cc}^+$ binding energy yield this result. This finding differs from earlier predictions of a bound state and motivates searches for the $T_{ss}$ at facilities such as the High Intensity heavy Ion Accelerator Facility (HIAF). This framework could be extended to other hadron-hadron channels to extract scattering observables and pole positions.

hep-lat.title: Muon and Tau Anomalies and $Δα_{had}^{(5)} (M_Z^2)$ in the Standard Model
hep-lat.author: Stephan Narison(LUPM, CNRS-IN2P3 and Univ.Montpellier - FR and iHEPMAD, Univ. Antananarivo - MG)
hep-lat.abstract: I review the present status of the Standard Model (SM) determination of the muon anomaly by emphasizing the estimate of the lowest hadronic vacuum polarization contributions using recent $e^+e^-$ data on $2\pi$ and $3\pi$ and the inclusive ratio $R^{ee}$ of total cross-sections compiled by PDG to which we add the QCD continuum including HO PT QCD up to $\alpha_s^5$, quark mass $m_q^2$ up to $\alpha_s^3$, $m_s^4$ up to $\alpha_s^2$ and QCD condensates. Adding the $e^+e^-\to \pi^0\gamma + \eta\gamma$ contributions to the CMD3 data, one obtains\,: $a_\mu\vert^{hvp}_{lo}=(7094\pm 37)\times 10^{-11}$. Combining this LO result with the HO estimate of the hadronic, QED and EW contributions, one obtains\,: $\Delta a_\mu^{sm} \equiv (a_\mu^{exp}-a_\mu^{sm})= (86\pm 38_{th}\pm 14.5_{exp})\times 10^{-11} $. The average of the recent estimates quoted in Table\,3 [$\oplus$ attempt to fit all $\,e^+e^-$ data] gives\,: $\Delta a_\mu^{sm} = (84.9[90.0]\pm 21.3_{th}\pm 14.5_{exp})\times 10^{-11}$\,. These results agree with the precise BMW20 lattice one and still suggest a window for new physics beyond the SM of $(2.1\sim 3.5)\,\sigma$. Besides some future projects for improving the $e^+e^-$ data, the MUonE for extracting directly $a_\mu^{tot}\vert^{hvp}_{lo}$ and J-PARC (E34) for an independent measurement of $a_\mu$, it is important to improve the Lattice results shown in Fig.\,9 which (at first sight) disagree each others despite the large errors and may question the reliability of the {\it averages of different averages} used in the White Paper (WP25) Our analysis is completed by updating the estimate of the hadronic contribution to the tau anomaly\,: $a_\tau\vert^{hvp}_{lo}=(3516\pm 25)\times 10^{-9}$ and to $\alpha(M_Z)\,: \,\Delta \alpha_{had}^{(5)} (M_Z^2)= (2770.7\pm 4.5)\times 10^{-5}. $

hep-lat.title: Thermal deep inelastic scattering, universality and complex geodesics
hep-lat.author: Andrei Parnachev
hep-lat.abstract: In deep inelastic scattering (DIS), a lepton scatters off a target hadron whose structure is probed by an exchanged photon with large spacelike virtuality. We consider two-point functions of currents in strongly interacting quantum field theories at finite temperature in this kinematic regime and use a holographic description to compute them. At large virtuality, the crossover from vacuum-dominated to thermally dominated physics corresponds to a transition from exponentially suppressed absorption to power-law behavior of the response functions. This regime is related to a particular near-lightcone limit of thermal CFT correlators. We show that the response functions exhibit a large degree of universality: the dependence on the three-point couplings of currents to the stress tensor enters through a channel-dependent coefficient multiplying the kinematic parameter that controls the relative size of vacuum and thermal effects. The same coefficient controls conformal collider bounds; when either bound is saturated, the corresponding response function takes its vacuum form in the near-lightcone limit. Furthermore, the absorption exponent in the low-temperature regime is related to a complex geodesic propagating in the near-lightcone geometry.

hep-lat.title: Deep Learning for Physicists: From Linear Regression to Reasoning Models
hep-lat.author: Masanori Hanada
hep-lat.abstract: These lecture notes are based on an introductory course on neural networks and deep learning that the author taught in the School of Mathematical Sciences at Queen Mary University of London in 2023/24 and 2024/25. The author, however, is a physicist, and it shows: wherever possible, ideas are explained with physical intuition rather than heavy formalism. Readers with a background in physics or mathematics who want a self-contained, introductory route into modern machine learning may therefore find these notes particularly friendly.The notes start from maximum likelihood, least squares, linear regression and (stochastic) gradient descent. They then cover neural networks, backpropagation, the vanishing gradient problem, batch and layer normalization, overfitting and regularization, adversarial examples, and the kernel method. The second half turns to natural language processing: word embeddings, recurrent networks and LSTMs, the attention mechanism and Transformers, and large language models, including scaling laws, the history of GPT, instruction tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback, hallucination, alignment faking, chain-of-thought reasoning and test-time scaling. The emphasis on large language models reflects requests from the students.The notes are aimed at third- and fourth-year students in the UK system. Because the course was also taken by students from other departments, very little is assumed: even basic material such as matrix multiplication is explained from scratch, so readers familiar with it can safely skip such parts. No originality is claimed; the aim is a coherent, intuitive path through the material. Developments after spring 2025 are not covered, but the basic ideas emphasized here are unlikely to go out of date soon.

hep-lat.title: Heavy double-gluon quarkonium and $\overline{b}ggc$ mesons
hep-lat.author: G. Daylan Esmer, B. Barsbay, K. Azizi, H. Sundu, S. Türkmen
hep-lat.abstract: We investigate heavy double-gluon hybrid mesons, built from a heavy quark-antiquark pair and two valence gluons, using the two-point QCD sum rule method. The charmonium-like $\bar{c}GGc$ and bottomonium-like $\bar{b}GGb$ states are considered with $J^{PC}=0^{\pm\pm}$ and $1^{\pm\pm}$, whereas the open-flavor $\bar{b}GGc$ states are classified by $J^{P}=0^{\pm}$ and $1^{\pm}$. The currents with $J^{PC}=0^{+-}, 0^{--}, 1^{++}$, and $1^{-+}$ vanish identically, so sum rules are derived for the remaining four channels. The operator product expansion is carried out up to dimension twelve, and the Borel parameter and continuum threshold are fixed so that the pole contribution dominates and the OPE converges. The resulting masses lie in the ranges $M\simeq 6.2$--$6.7$~GeV for $\bar{c}GGc$, $M\simeq 12.0$--$12.2$~GeV for $\bar{b}GGb$, and $M\simeq 9.2$--$9.6$~GeV for $\bar{b}GGc$, and the current couplings are obtained for all channels. These predictions provide a basis for analyzing the strong decays of double-gluon hybrids and for interpreting future experimental data in the heavy-quark sector.

hep-lat.title: First Lattice Calculation of Structure-Dependent Radiative Corrections to Lepton-Flavor-Universality Ratios in Leptonic Decays
hep-lat.author: Peter Boyle, Norman H. Christ, Xu Feng, Taku Izubuchi, Luchang Jin, Christopher T. Sachrajda, Xin-Yu Tuo
hep-lat.abstract: The ratio of electronic to muonic leptonic decay widths, $R_{e/\mu}$, for the light mesons $\pi$ and $K$, provides a clean test of lepton flavor universality (LFU) and a sensitive probe of physics beyond the Standard Model. Its Standard-Model prediction is exceptionally precise, with the leading uncertainty associated with the structure-dependent (SD) radiative correction of $O(0.1\%)$. As experiments such as PIONEER and NA62 aim for unprecedented precision, this SD correction has become an essential ingredient in precision experiment--theory comparisons. We present the first lattice QCD$+$QED calculation of this SD correction at the physical pion mass and in the continuum limit. We employ the infinite-volume reconstruction (IVR) method with Coulomb-gauge photons, significantly reducing both statistical errors and finite-volume effects. We obtain the Standard-Model predictions, $R_{e/\mu}=1.23516(10)\times10^{-4}$ for $\pi$ and $R_{e/\mu}=2.47661(31)\times10^{-5}$ for $K$. Our results reduce the hadronic uncertainty in $R_{e/\mu}$, provide the most precise Standard-Model predictions to date, and establish first-principles benchmarks for future high-precision tests of LFU.

hep-lat.title: Searching for symmetric mass generation with staggered fermions in four dimensions
hep-lat.author: Nouman Butt, Simon Catterall, Gwen Hartshaw, Anna Hasenfratz
hep-lat.abstract: We conduct numerical simulations to map out the phase diagram and critical behavior of a lattice Higgs model composed of two massless staggered fermion fields forming a doublet under a global $SU(2)$ and coupled to a scalar field in the adjoint representation of the group. The scalar action consists of a potential comprising quadratic and quartic terms and a scalar kinetic term. At fixed quartic coupling we explore a two-dimensional parameter space finding a massless symmetric phase at weak coupling and a massive symmetric phase (SMG phase) at strong coupling. An intermediate anti-ferromagnetic phase separates these two regimes. These results are consistent with leading order weak and strong coupling expansions. We find that the critical lines bounding the intermediate phase merge at a unique point where all fermion bilinear condensates vanish but fermion susceptibilities diverge as non-trivial powers of the lattice size. We conjecture that this merged point corresponds to a multicritical point and may describe a phase consisting of a condensate of certain topological defects.

hep-lat.title: Quark-mass dependence of two-nucleon scattering
hep-lat.author: Jorge Baeza-Ballesteros, André Baião-Raposo, Davide Laudicina, Malcolm Lazarow, Thomas R. Richardson, Miguel Salg, John Bulava, M.A. Clark, Jeremy R. Green, Andrew Hanlon, Renwick J. Hudspith, Daniel Mohler, Colin Morningstar, Amy Nicholson, Fernando Romero-López, André Walker-Loud, Hartmut Wittig(for the Baryon Scattering Collaboration)
hep-lat.abstract: Understanding how the properties of the visible Universe depend on the parameters of the Standard Model of particle physics requires \emph{ab initio} theoretical computations. To that end, we investigate the quark-mass dependence of low-energy nucleon-nucleon scattering in the deuteron and dineutron channels. We perform lattice-QCD calculations at pion masses $M_\pi\approx 200$ and $280$ MeV and compare their results to phenomenology at the physical point and to a previous calculation at $M_\pi\approx 710$ MeV. Scattering amplitudes, phase shifts, and threshold parameters are determined from finite-volume spectra using quantization conditions that explicitly incorporate long-distance effects from one-pion exchange. We analyze the pion-mass dependence of scattering lengths and effective ranges using chiral effective field theory with Weinberg and Kaplan-Savage-Wise power countings. From this, we estimate the pion-mass derivatives of the inverse scattering lengths and binding momentum, at the physical point. Both power countings indicate that the deuteron unbinds near $M_\pi\approx 220$ MeV.

hep-lat.title: Numerical tests of chiral fermion weights with $η$-invariant phases in the 3450 model
hep-lat.author: Tatsuhiro Misumi
hep-lat.abstract: We test numerically a recently proposed prescription for coupling continuum chiral fermions to interpolated lattice gauge fields, in which the fermion weight has a Pauli-Villars (PV) regularized magnitude and a phase given by an Atiyah-Patodi-Singer (APS) $\eta$-invariant in one higher dimension. We use the anomaly-free two-dimensional $U(1)$ theory with left-handed charges $3,4$ and right-handed charges $5,0$, whose torus determinant is known exactly. At zero magnetic flux, with gauge fields interpolated from lattice links, the Polyakov loops evaluated on a $16\times16$ grid of flat connections agree with the exact values within $0.04\%$, whereas omitting the APS phase substantially reduces them to about $3\%$ of the exact result. The vacuum-polarization response yields an induced mass $m/e=2.82089$, close to $5/\sqrt{\pi}=2.82095$. At unit flux, where zero modes make the determinant vanish, we calculate a twelve-point correlator on a cylinder with the generalized APS boundary condition. For three smooth backgrounds its magnitude agrees with the exact result within $0.8\%$. Without the $\eta$-invariant its phase deviates by $1.8$-$3.0$ mrad, and with it by $0.2$-$0.5$ mrad. The phase of each charged fermion changes by $15$-$46$ mrad when the gauge field is extended differently into the third dimension, but the change cancels to below $0.2$ mrad in the anomaly-free combination.

hep-lat.title: Hamiltonian Truncation Framework for Gauge Theories on the Interval
hep-lat.author: Rachel Houtz, James Ingoldby
hep-lat.abstract: In this work, we investigate gauge theories in two dimensions nonperturbatively using the Hamiltonian truncation approach. Working on a spatial interval and adopting the axial gauge, we remove all gauge field degrees of freedom and express the interacting Hamiltonian in the eigenbasis of the free Dirac theory, truncated at a finite energy. As a benchmark we analyse the Schwinger model, where our numerical spectra agree closely with the exact results from bosonization across a wide range of couplings, validating the construction of the Hamiltonian. We then generalize the formulation to nonabelian gauge groups and apply it to SU(3) gauge theory with a single massless Dirac fermion. These results demonstrate that gauge theories can be explored nonperturbatively using a truncated Hamiltonian that generates evolutions in ordinary time, offering a complementary alternative to lattice field theory.

hep-lat.title: Axial-Vector Lattice Benchmarks Reveal a Common Medium Response of Meson Screening in Hot QCD
hep-lat.author: Jie Ren, Chen Chen, Fei Gao, Si-xue Qin
hep-lat.abstract: Meson screening masses trace the evolution of hadronic correlations toward quasi-free quark--antiquark screening in hot QCD. Combining lattice QCD (LQCD) benchmarks with a symmetry-preserving Dyson--Schwinger baseline, we identify a flavor-dependent axial-vector quasi-free onset, $x^\ast_{fg}=T^\ast_{fg}/T_c$: an operational matching scale based on the proximity of the axial-vector screening mass to its free-field reference, where $T_c$ is the pseudocritical temperature. On the finite interval $1\le T/T_c\lesssim x^\ast_{fg}$, independent light/strange and charm-containing lattice benchmarks are organized by a common medium-response function with one flavor-sector parameter. One axial-vector point fixes this parameter; the remaining axial-vector data test the temperature dependence of the response, and vector screening masses validate it without vector input. A reduced-mass interpolation then yields lattice-testable predictions for quasi-free onset scales and vector and axial-vector screening spectra in light--charm and open-bottom sectors.

hep-lat.title: Flavour decomposition of the chiral-odd form factors of the nucleon
hep-lat.author: U. Özdem
hep-lat.abstract: We compute the chiral-odd form factors $H_T$, $E_T$ and $\tilde{H}_T$ of the nucleon within light-cone QCD sum rules, separately for the $u$ and $d$ quarks, over $1\le Q^2\le 10$ GeV$^2$, and organise their values at $Q^2=0$ into the tensor monopole, dipole and quadrupole moments $g_T$, $\kappa_T$ and $Q_T$. The flavour components of the quadrupole moment and the isoscalar channel have not previously been obtained in this framework. The form factors are read from a basis of Lorentz structures that becomes independent only after a canonical ordering of the Dirac strings, and three of the eight surviving structures give the three form factors separately. Two statements follow from the analytic expressions. The $d$-quark contributions to $E_T$ and $\tilde{H}_T$ are equal and opposite in the chiral limit, the breaking being proportional to the quark mass and to the twist-six amplitude $\mathcal{V}_6$. At the level of the least suppressed momentum-fraction integral, the isoscalar tensor charge receives no leading-twist contribution, the twist-three terms of the two flavours cancelling. Neither statement is visible without resolving the flavours. At $\mu^2=1$ GeV$^2$ we obtain, for the two distribution-amplitude sets, $g_T^{u-d}=1.27(7)$ and $1.08(6)$, $\kappa_T^{u-d}=1.35(62)$ and $1.58(59)$, $Q_T^{u-d}=-4.40(83)$ and $-4.20(73)$, $g_T^{u+d}=0.39(7)$ and $0.38(6)$, $\kappa_T^{u+d}=4.47(62)$ and $4.32(59)$, and $Q_T^{u+d}=2.41(53)$ and $1.56(30)$. The mean-field relation $2\tilde{H}_T^{u-d}=-E_T^{u-d}$ holds in sign and in order of magnitude, the ratio being $0.64(16)$ and $0.67(15)$. In the impact-parameter plane the two flavour distributions are displaced in opposite transverse directions by nearly equal amounts, $\langle b_y\rangle=0.37$ and $-0.37$ fm, and both are elongated across the polarisation axis, the $d$ quark some five to six times more strongly than the $u$ quark.

hep-th.title: Schwarzschild scattering from CFT
hep-th.author: Paolo Arnaudo, Benjamin Withers
hep-th.abstract: We show that retarded CFT correlators on $\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{S}^2$ in a state described by the small black hole in AdS$_4$ can be used to derive asymptotically flat Schwarzschild partial-wave S-matrix elements, including its spectrum of quasinormal modes. This is achieved by identifying a class of operators for which the dual bulk fields behave as plane waves near the AdS boundary for sufficiently high frequencies. For such operators there is a simple analytic relation between CFT correlators and reflection coefficients which behaves gracefully in the flat space limit, $L\to \infty$. These include spin-1, spin-2, and conformally coupled scalars. We provide a simple toy model that captures how dissipative QNMs can appear for short times inside Hermitian systems, closely resembling the small black hole in AdS.

hep-th.title: Gravitational Memory Correlators and BMS Symmetry
hep-th.author: Enrico Herrmann, Ian Moult, Brett Oertel, Julio Parra-Martinez, Biswajit Sahoo
hep-th.abstract: We compute the n-point memory and mixed energy-memory correlators for scalar decay into gravitons using the in-in formalism at leading order in perturbative quantum gravity. We obtain compact results for arbitrary n and explicitly verify the supertranslation flux balance relation between memory, energy, and Bondi mass detectors, realizing asymptotic symmetry constraints on infrared-finite observables.

hep-th.title: Rational conformal interfaces between the Ising and tricritical Ising models from a tetrality web
hep-th.author: António Antunes, Jin Chen, Junchen Rong
hep-th.abstract: We construct rational conformal interfaces between the Ising and tricritical Ising (TIM) models by using different chiral symmetries to prepare their folded boundary states. We use a moving up procedure which extends the product theory to an auxiliary coset with an $S_3$ automorphism group, where permutations give twisted Cardy states. We complement this with a moving down approach which reduces to the $S_3$ invariant algebra. Overall, these procedures uncover a tetrality web relating four different theories. Pulling back ordinary Cardy states of the smallest theory in the web to the physical tensor product system gives eighteen factorized interfaces and six transmitting interfaces. The latter agree with four transposition and two 3-cycle twisted boundaries in the largest theory. They include Gaiotto's RG wall and the interface obtained by fusing an Ising duality line into it. The six interfaces carry the regular action of the TIM fusion ring and have the same energy transmission coefficient, $35/48$. Their boundary entropies, bulk correlations and operator spectra distinguish them. We calculate these observables and the complete annulus amplitudes between the twenty four boundaries.

hep-th.title: Constants and Nonperturbative Corrections in $V^{5,2}$ Theories
hep-th.author: Seyed Morteza Hosseini
hep-th.abstract: We study perturbative and exponentially small corrections to the on-shell effective twisted superpotentials of two three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ theories associated with free and fixed-locus cyclic quotients of the non-toric Sasaki-Einstein manifold $V^{5,2}$. These are the two-node Chern-Simons theory at levels $(k,-k)$ and the one-node flavored theory with $N_f$ fundamental pairs, respectively. At superconformal chemical potentials, we propose the Chern-Simons counterpart of the all-order perturbative expression for the flavored theory and obtain convergent integral representations for the rank-independent constants of both theories. At integer parameters, these constants admit explicit evaluations involving finite sums of Clausen functions and $\zeta(3)$, while their large-parameter expansions Borel sum to the defining integrals. At $k=1,3$ and $N_f=1,3$, we conjecture complete exponential remainders expressed through Eichler integrals of weight-four Eisenstein series. Supported by high-precision Bethe solutions, the resulting completions coincide at unit quotient order but differ at order three. We determine the minimal modular levels of the Eisenstein generators and establish convergence and natural boundaries for their primitives. Within the relative M-theory localization prescription, a complementary bulk analysis recovers the Chern-Simons shifted rank and constant in the $b\to0^+$ limit of the squashed-sphere partition function. We propose a generalization incorporating fixed-locus contributions that yields the corresponding flavored-theory result. The two theories therefore share a modular structure in their nonperturbative coefficient laws, but distinct perturbative shifts and exponential corrections resolve differences invisible in their common leading $N^{3/2}$ behavior.

hep-th.title: Quadratic Sum Rules for Scalar Amplitudes
hep-th.author: Karol Kampf, Jiří Novotný, David Podivín, Jonah Stalknecht
hep-th.abstract: Kleiss--Kuijf and Bern--Carrasco--Johansson relations, and their string monodromy generalizations, have long provided some of the most powerful and useful constraints on partial amplitudes. Motivated by their success, we uncover a new class of quadratic-sum rules that connect scalar amplitudes at different multiplicities. Combining recursion, kinematic shifts, and symbolic regression, we establish them for the nonlinear sigma model and its string-inspired extensions. We then extend these relations to diagonal elements of the inverse Kawai--Lewellen--Tye matrix and subsequently to planar scalar theories with nonderivative interactions and general propagators.

hep-th.title: Generalised global symmetries of 6d SCFTs on a circle from the blow-up equations
hep-th.author: William Harding, Noppadol Mekareeya
hep-th.abstract: We study 6d $(1,0)$ SCFTs on a circle, possibly twisted, through the blow-up equations of their 5d descriptions. For every theory we consider, we construct the explicit map between the 6d and 5d frames, including the ratio $r$ of the Kaluza--Klein (KK) mass to the instanton mass, which depends on the frame and not only on the twist. Our main result is that the higher-form symmetries of these theories, their mixed anomalies and 2-groups can all be read off from the fluxes through the exceptional curve of the blown-up $\mathbb{C}^2$. The flux sectors are the 't$~$Hooft sectors of the 5d 1-form symmetries. On the tensor fluxes, the 6d Green--Schwarz couplings fix the weights, whose fractional exponents we read as the mixed anomalies of the 6d 2-form symmetry with the KK $\mathrm{U}(1)$, gravity, flavour and $\mathrm{SU}(2)_R$. The fluxes forced in each sector decide between a 2-group and a mixed anomaly. For instance, the twisted frames $\mathfrak{su}(4)_{0,4}+4\Lambda^2$ carry a non-split $\mathbb{Z}_4$ 2-group, while, in $\mathfrak{su}(4)_2+4\Lambda^2$ and $\mathfrak{su}(4)_6+2\Lambda^2$, the instanton symmetry is locked to the flavour centre and only a mixed anomaly remains. The same method applies to the $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ gauging of two, three and four copies of the $E_1$ theory, which describes, respectively, $\mathrm{SU}(4)_0$, pure $\mathrm{Spin}(8)$ and the untwisted $\mathfrak{so}(8)$ KK theory. There, the fluxes exhibit the extensions of 1-form symmetries inherited from the $E_1$ 2-groups, identify the states that break each accidental 1-form symmetry and the background to which it is locked, and give the 5d 2-group to which the $S_3$-invariant 6d 3-group reduces.

hep-th.title: Non-Topological Chiral Anomaly: The Chiral Magnetoelectric Effect
hep-th.author: Rémy Larue, Amaury Marchon, Jérémie Quevillon, Diego Saviot
hep-th.abstract: We derive the chiral anomaly in a thermal medium and show that, in addition to the well-established topological piece, the anomaly acquires a previously overlooked non-topological contribution, relevant for non-gauged axial symmetries. Remarkably, this modification of the continuity equation is independent of the electromagnetic fields, thereby giving rise to novel transport effects in relativistic hydrodynamics. We further propose an experimentally accessible new effect in Weyl semimetals which we call the Chiral Magnetoelectric Effect: an electric field proportional to the magnetic field is generated by the non-topological anomaly, even in the absence of an externally applied electric field. Beyond this concrete prediction, our results establish a broader hydrodynamic framework for non-topological chiral anomalies, opening the door to a range of previously unexplored anomaly-induced transport phenomena across condensed-matter and high-energy systems.

hep-th.title: A Bound on Wormhole Probing Time from Holographic Multi-Entropy
hep-th.author: Takanori Anegawa, Norihiro Iizuka
hep-th.abstract: Bipartite entanglement entropy eventually saturates and therefore cannot track the continued growth of an eternal wormhole. Recently, it was shown that genuine tripartite multi-entropy can probe wormhole growth even after bipartite entanglement entropies have saturated. This naturally raises the question: can increasing the number of parties extend the probing time indefinitely? Adopting the multiway maximin prescription and assuming that its selected representatives are regular spacetime-stationary networks, we prove that the answer is no for nonrotating BTZ black holes. We establish a common finite upper bound on the probing time for every fixed finite boundary partition, independent of the number, sizes, and arrangement of its parties. For any network on any Cauchy slice, there exists a comparison network that assigns the entire central region containing the wormhole interior to a single party. A network longer than this comparison network cannot minimize length on that slice. The central length required by a stationary network connecting the two boundaries grows with time, whereas the central length of the comparison network remains uniformly bounded. At sufficiently late times, such a network therefore cannot minimize length on any Cauchy slice containing it and is excluded from the maximin prescription. Consequently, beyond this bound, no network selected by maximin enters the black-hole interior.

hep-th.title: Projected DKP spin-1 sectors in a $(2+1)$-dimensional static wormhole: Self-duality, helicity content, and spectral correspondence
hep-th.author: Luis B. Castro
hep-th.abstract: We use the projected spin-1 Duffin--Kemmer--Petiau (DKP) equation in $2+1$ dimensions to clarify the physical content of the irreducible $3\times3$ representations. The projected antisymmetric tensor is algebraically dual to the projected vector, and the two twin representations select conjugate self-dual covariant-curl sectors, which reduce to opposite massive helicities in the flat-space limit. We then apply this structure to the static wormhole problem previously studied with a single irreducible representation. The first-order radial DKP system contains an exceptional normalizable bound-state branch at $\omega^2=M^2$ that is absent from the master-variable reduction, whereas the generic master and circular sectors are related by a Darboux transformation. The latter preserves the transmission and reflection probabilities, while the quasinormal modes are organized into two pole families in the complex radial-momentum plane, leading to the physical pairing $(\omega,-\omega^*)$ rather than a global $\pm\omega$ prescription.

hep-th.title: Stochastic gauge fixing from the holographic renormalization group
hep-th.author: Soner Albayrak
hep-th.abstract: We extend the dictionary between stochastic quantization and holographic Wilsonian renormalization to Yang-Mills theory in four-dimensional anti-de Sitter space at tree level. The radial component of the bulk gauge field is Zwanziger's gauge-fixing function; radial gauge is Parisi-Wu quantization, whose random walk of gauge modes is the longitudinal bulk propagator. We obtain the triple- and quadruple-trace couplings of gluons at finite cutoff in closed form. On transverse data, their dependence on the bulk gauge resides in a single zero mode, which drops out of the flat-space limit.

hep-th.title: Conditional Principle of Least Action: Gauge Algebra and Noether's Second Theorem
hep-th.author: V. A. Abakumova, S. L. Lyakhovich
hep-th.abstract: We consider the problem of a conditional extremum of an action within a class of fields constrained by differential equations. For this setup, we establish the interconnection between the gauge symmetry algebra of the equations constraining the admissible fields and that of the action restricted to this class of fields. Based on this relation between the two gauge algebras, we derive an extension of Noether's second theorem and its converse. The general method is illustrated by the example of linearized gravity with the Einstein-Hilbert action and the class of admissible metrics restricted by the Cotton equation.

hep-th.title: Classification of Conformal Ising/Tricritical Ising Interfaces Preserving $\mathcal{W}_3^{\mathbb{Z}_2}$ Symmetry
hep-th.author: Bufan Zheng
hep-th.abstract: We classify conformal interfaces between the Ising and tricritical Ising models that preserve the chiral algebra $\mathcal{W}_3^{\mathbb{Z}_2}$. Using the folding trick, we formulate the problem in terms of boundary states satisfying the Cardy condition and determine the unique NIM-rep compatible with the bulk partition function. We obtain a complete set of 24 fundamental boundary states, of which 18 correspond to factorized interfaces preserving the full product Virasoro symmetry, while the remaining six break this symmetry. We construct these six interfaces explicitly and determine their annulus partition functions. They are related by topological defect line dressings, and one coincides with the RG domain wall proposed by Gaiotto.

hep-th.title: Large-$N$ expansion in SU($N$) Yang-Mills-like theories
hep-th.author: Marco Bochicchio, Mauro Papinutto, Francesco Scardino
hep-th.abstract: It has been known for fifty years that bare U($N$) pure Yang-Mills (YM) theory admits the large-$N$ 't Hooft expansion for the $n$-point connected correlators of gauge-invariant single-trace operators, where the corresponding Feynman diagrams are topologically classified by the sum over the genus $g$ of $n$-punctured smooth orientable closed Riemann surfaces. In fact, 't Hooft expansion extends verbatim to U($N$) YM-like theories whose Lagrangians only involve fields valued in the U($N$) Lie algebra - including supersymmetric (SUSY) extensions of pure YM theory such as $\mathcal{N}=1,4$ SUSY YM. The aim of the present paper is to systematically work out the topology of the large-$N$ expansion in SU($N$) - as opposed to U($N$) - YM-like theories, where a number of subtleties inevitably arise. Indeed, since the U($1$) inside the U($N$) YM-like theories decouples, the large-$N$ U($N$) and SU($N$) expansions should either essentially coincide or intrinsically differ - in the latter case necessarily by extra - possibly singular - topologies, as the 't Hooft expansion in U($N$) YM-like theories already exhausts all the smooth topologies. In fact, we demonstrate that 't Hooft smooth topologies are actually generically incomplete in the large-$N$ expansion of both the SU($N$) and renormalized U($N$) YM-like theories, where renormalization inevitably separates the SU($N$) sector that is interacting from the U($1$) sector that is free. Specifically, we interpret the extra topologies that arise in SU($N$) theories for correlators of higher-twist quasi-partonic operators as singular pinched closed surfaces, thus extending our previous investigation of correlators of twist-$2$ operators for which extra pinched tori arise.

hep-th.title: The $\mathbb{Z}_2$ twist line defect of the 3D Ising CFT on the fuzzy sphere from multi-target density matrix renormalization group
hep-th.author: Jing-Hao Jin, Yang Qi
hep-th.abstract: The fuzzy-sphere regularization provides a powerful framework for studying three-dimensional (3D) conformal field theories (CFTs) through radial quantization, but conformal defects have so far been studied with it only by exact diagonalization (ED) of small systems. In this work we realize the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ twist line defect of the 3D Ising CFT on the fuzzy sphere by imposing antiperiodic boundary conditions on the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-odd fermion flavor, and solve it with a multi-target density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) algorithm that optimizes several low-lying states of each symmetry sector in a common matrix-product basis. This gives the defect spectrum at system sizes well beyond the reach of ED (up to $2s+1=25$, or $49$ spinless orbitals). The spectrum obeys the spin-parity selection rule of the twist line and organizes into conformal multiplets along the line. Using the displacement operator as an intrinsic ruler, its protected descendant as a test, and the bulk stress tensor as an independent cross-check, we identify the leading finite-size corrections and obtain controlled continuum extrapolations, which sharpen the dimensions of several known defect primaries and resolve four higher-lying ones. This study establishes the fuzzy sphere combined with multi-target DMRG as a framework for precision studies of conformal defects.

hep-th.title: Holographic Entanglement after a Global Quench in Noncommutative Yang-Mills Theory
hep-th.author: Elahe Hassanpour, Komeil Babaei Velni, M. Reza Mohammadi Mozaffar
hep-th.abstract: The time evolution of holographic entanglement entropy and mixed-state correlations following a global quench in four-dimensional N=4 noncommutative Yang-Mills theory is investigated using a Vaidya geometry. For strip-shaped regions extended along a noncommutative direction, two distinct early-time growth regimes emerge, depending on the relation between the shell-crossing and noncommutative scales: logarithmic growth, with a coefficient proportional to the injected energy density and the square of the noncommutative scale, followed by quadratic growth. For sufficiently wide strips, an intermediate linear-growth regime appears, governed by an entanglement velocity that increases with noncommutativity. The approach to equilibrium is also examined, revealing the role of the butterfly velocity in the continuous evolution of extremal surfaces, while competing branches can modify the physical saturation time. For two disjoint strips, the leading width-independent logarithmic contribution cancels in the mutual information, whereas the entanglement wedge cross section exhibits an intermediate linear-growth regime governed by the same entanglement velocity, provided the connected entanglement wedge remains dominant.

hep-th.title: On the Spontaneous symmetry breaking of Conformal Gravity to Weyl and Einstein Gravities
hep-th.author: Partha Nandi, Gerasimos Kouniatalis, Stelios Stefas, George Zoupanos
hep-th.abstract: Does the special-conformal connection remain an auxiliary field when a spontaneously broken conformal gauge theory is promoted to a fully dynamical Yang-Mills-Higgs theory, and under what conditions does its elimination yield Weyl gravity? We address these questions within an $\mathrm{SO}(2,4)$ gauge-theoretic formulation of gravity. Revisiting the gravitational sector selected by spontaneous symmetry breaking through an adjoint $15$-plet, we retain the special-conformal connection as an independent field and demonstrate that, on a source-free projected branch, its algebraic equation of motion determines it in terms of the Schouten tensor. Eliminating this connection yields the four-dimensional Weyl-squared action, up to the Euler density, without imposing the Schouten relation as an additional geometrical constraint. We then extend the analysis to the standard local Yang-Mills-Higgs theory and show that the special-conformal connection remains auxiliary, owing to the structure of the invariant bilinear form of $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$, which prevents the appearance of an independent kinetic operator. The additional gauge and scalar sectors can modify its algebraic solution, so the exact Weyl reduction is restricted to the source-free branch. We further investigate the linearised spectrum of the reduced Weyl theory around de Sitter spacetime, identifying massless and partially massless spin-2 branches, with the latter occurring at $m_{\mathrm{PM}}^2=2\Lambda/3$. Finally, we discuss the subsequent symmetry breaking induced by an antisymmetric scalar $6$-plet and its role in connecting the Weyl-gravity phase to Einstein gravity.

hep-th.title: The Goldstone--Wilczek Charge on the Rim
hep-th.author: Laurence A. Jacobs
hep-th.abstract: A solenoid flux $\Phi=2\pi\alpha$ threaded through the center of the Kaplan--Sen lattice disk binds a ground-state charge $Q_{\rm core}=\alpha-\mathrm{round}(\alpha)$, and the edge carries exactly the opposite charge. The edge charge is the Goldstone--Wilczek charge of the edge ladder, $Q_{\rm edge}=-\tfrac12\eta$, with $\eta$ its spectral asymmetry. At $\Phi=\pi$ one unit of charge crosses the disk. We ask how the rim operator, the Schur complement of the disk Hamiltonian on its boundary sites, registers this transfer. Its count of negative eigenvalues never changes over the flux cycle. Instead, the unit of charge enters the rim through a simple pole: the extremal eigenvalue of the rim operator passes through infinity in the same flux interval as the charge jump, with $\Delta Q_{\rm edge}=\tfrac12\Delta\,\mathrm{sign}\,\lambda_{\rm ext}$. The residue factorizes into the coupling of the inner edge mode to the rim and the inverse slope of that mode's level, and grows linearly with the radius. All statements are checked numerically on disks of radius $R=11$, $19$ and $34$.

hep-th.title: Local field shifts and the Gribov-Zwanziger horizon functional
hep-th.author: Daniel Guimaraes Tedesco
hep-th.abstract: We study a Maggiore-Schaden-like re-centering of the Gribov-Zwanziger action using a smooth compactly supported profile. At fixed background and finite cutoff, under the stated coercivity and contour hypotheses, this transformation preserves the original horizon functional with no residual dependence on the profile. The extension to gauge-field integration requires additional domination assumptions. Near a self-adjoint first Gribov horizon, the response depends on both the lowest Faddeev-Popov eigenvalue and its source weight. We extend this visibility analysis to non-self-adjoint compressions, separating source darkness from truncation-induced shielding, and recall continuum transverse $SU(2)$ examples. Transporting the composite insertion preserves the regulated Gaussian and resolvent structure.
