hep-th.title: Torsional Hall Viscosity of Massive Chern Insulators: Finite Temperature and Chemical Potential
hep-th.author: Weizhen Jia, Ioannis Matthaiakakis, David Rodríguez Fernández, Zhuo-Yu Xian, Johanna Erdmenger, Ewelina M. Hankiewicz, René Meyer
hep-th.abstract: We study the torsional Hall viscosity $\zeta_{\rm H}$ of Chern insulators at finite temperature and chemical potential. Our analysis considers the massive Dirac fermion and two deformations: a constant out-of-plane magnetic field and a momentum-dependent mass described by the single-block Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang (BHZ) Hamiltonian. For the massive Dirac theory, we show that temperature and chemical potential lead to UV-finite corrections and that a chemical potential outside the bulk gap modifies $\zeta_{\rm H}$ even at zero temperature. In a constant magnetic field, the response of massive Dirac fermions is dictated by the relativistic Landau-level spectrum, leading to a plateau structure at zero temperature that is smoothed at finite temperature. The jumps are proportional to the Dirac mass and inversely proportional to the squared magnetic length and the newly occupied Landau-level energy. Finally, we present a detailed study of the correction to $\zeta_{\rm H}$ in the single-block BHZ continuum model due to temperature and chemical potential. For parameters relevant to (Hg,Mn)Te quantum wells, the magnitude of the jump across a mass domain wall retains its vacuum enhancement due to the BHZ deformation as long as the chemical potential lies sufficiently deep inside the gap compared with the thermal energy. Our results extend the theory of torsional Hall viscosity to experimentally relevant conditions and may facilitate its future detection.

hep-th.title: Deep Learning for Physicists: From Linear Regression to Reasoning Models
hep-th.author: Masanori Hanada
hep-th.abstract: These lecture notes are based on an introductory course on neural networks and deep learning that the author taught in the School of Mathematical Sciences at Queen Mary University of London in 2023/24 and 2024/25. The author, however, is a physicist, and it shows: wherever possible, ideas are explained with physical intuition rather than heavy formalism. Readers with a background in physics or mathematics who want a self-contained, introductory route into modern machine learning may therefore find these notes particularly friendly.The notes start from maximum likelihood, least squares, linear regression and (stochastic) gradient descent. They then cover neural networks, backpropagation, the vanishing gradient problem, batch and layer normalization, overfitting and regularization, adversarial examples, and the kernel method. The second half turns to natural language processing: word embeddings, recurrent networks and LSTMs, the attention mechanism and Transformers, and large language models, including scaling laws, the history of GPT, instruction tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback, hallucination, alignment faking, chain-of-thought reasoning and test-time scaling. The emphasis on large language models reflects requests from the students.The notes are aimed at third- and fourth-year students in the UK system. Because the course was also taken by students from other departments, very little is assumed: even basic material such as matrix multiplication is explained from scratch, so readers familiar with it can safely skip such parts. No originality is claimed; the aim is a coherent, intuitive path through the material. Developments after spring 2025 are not covered, but the basic ideas emphasized here are unlikely to go out of date soon.

hep-th.title: Detectability of Eccentric Intermediate Mass-Ratio Inspiral in the Decihertz Band
hep-th.author: Devesh Giri, Sajal Mukherjee, Apratim Ganguly, Sanjit Mitra
hep-th.abstract: The proposed decihertz gravitational-wave (GW) band $(\sim 10^{-2}-1\,\Hz)$ will observe the late inspiral of intermediate mass-ratio inspirals (IMRIs), binaries with mass ratios $10^2 \lesssim q \lesssim 10^4$ that assemble dynamically in dense stellar environments and are expected to retain measurable eccentricity. Search and parameter-estimation pipelines are predominantly built around circular templates, and we test this assumption. Using black-hole perturbation theory waveforms from \textsc{FastEMRIWaveforms} for a representative IMRI ($M=10^4\,\modot$, $q=100$, observed for its final $10\,\hr$), we compute fitting factors between eccentric signals and circular templates, maximizing over the template's total mass and mass ratio with a differential-evolution search, for the B-DECIGO, LGWA-Si, and IndIGO-D noise curves and a flat PSD. The mismatch grows with initial eccentricity $e_0$ and crosses the standard $3\%$ threshold at $e_0\simeq3\times10^{-2}$, well within the range allowed by the waveform model and expected from dynamical formation. The best-fitting circular templates also bias the total mass and mass ratio by several percent at $e_0=0.1$. Combining the mismatch with the signal-to-noise-dependent distinguishability criterion, we find that for a source at $1\,\mathrm{Gpc}$, eccentricities as small as $e_0\simeq5\times10^{-4}$ (B-DECIGO and IndIGO-D) and $5\times10^{-3}$ (LGWA-Si) are resolvable, one to two orders of magnitude below where detection efficiency degrades. The loss of match arises from the excitation of radial Teukolsky harmonics, which spread power into sidebands that circular templates cannot represent, and from the slower orbital decay of eccentric binaries at fixed initial semi-latus rectum. Robust detection and parameter estimation of IMRIs with DECIGO, LGWA, and IndIGO-D will require eccentric waveform models and template banks.

hep-th.title: Non-factorisable Yangian Lax matrices through oscillators
hep-th.author: Rouven Frassek, Henrik Jürgens
hep-th.abstract: We construct oscillator realisations of Yangian Lax operators in type $A$, with particular interest in non-factorisable operators associated with prime snake modules. Our construction applies to finite-dimensional skew representations of $Y(\mathfrak{gl}_n)$. We prove that these representations are generated by the tensor vacuum in suitably ordered tensor products of oscillator representations. Their Lax operators are obtained by restricting the corresponding products of linear oscillator Lax operators to these submodules. We determine the vacuum eigenvalues and Drinfeld polynomials, and give a determinant formula for the dimensions directly in terms of the highest loop weights. A $21$-dimensional example illustrates the construction, including an explicit basis and a transfer-matrix identity.

hep-th.title: Non-Canonical Q-balls in Polyattractor Inflation Models
hep-th.author: Kimberley Siret, Rhys Abercromby, Kit Lloyd-Stubbs, John McDonald
hep-th.abstract: We show that Q-balls can exist in supergravity-based polyattractor inflation models that interpolate between $\alpha$-attractor T-models and polynomial attractor models. We consider both the original polyattractor potential and a natural generalisation. We find that Q-balls solutions exist when the model deviates significantly from the T-model $\alpha$-attractor, whereas in the T-model limit no Q-balls exist. These are non-canonical Q-balls due to the non-canonical kinetic term of the complex inflaton field. Such Q-balls could have significant cosmological consequences if they are produced at the end of inflation. In particular, if the global $\mathrm{U}(1)$ symmetry of the supergravity-based polyattractor model is unbroken, the Q-balls can be absolutely stable and could account for dark matter.

hep-th.title: Geometry of squeezed states. The phase-space metric, relative vacua and cosmology
hep-th.author: Alejandro Corichi, Jerónimo Cortez
hep-th.abstract: Geometry enters quantum theory in two places. The space of quantum states carries a symplectic form, which generates unitary evolution, and a metric, which governs uncertainties and transition probabilities. The classical phase space acquires a metric of its own when a vacuum is chosen: quantizing a linear system amounts to choosing a compatible complex structure, equivalently a compatible metric $g$. We take this second metric as the primary object and show that it plays, on phase space, the role that the quantum metric plays on the space of states: fluctuations of linear observables are $g$-norms of Hamiltonian vector fields, and along coherent states $g/2\hbar$ \emph{is} the quantum metric. Squeezed states then have a simple description. A squeezed vacuum is the vacuum of another metric, and squeezing is a property of a pair of metrics, a relative vacuum, whose invariants are the eigenvalues $e^{\pm2r_i}$ of $L=g_0^{-1}g$. We work out the harmonic oscillator in detail, including why a rotated squeezed state no longer minimizes the product of the displayed uncertainties. Quadratic evolution deforms the metric, and only the part of the generator that is self-adjoint with respect to the reference changes the $r_i$, at a rate we give exactly. For fields, a vacuum is unitarily implementable relative to a reference exactly when it lies at finite distance from it in the space of vacua. For a massless field in de Sitter space we revisit the two canonical charts compared by Grain and Vennin: relative to the reference of the standard squeezing formalism the Bunch--Davies state has $\sinh r_k=1/(2|k\eta|)$, and relative to the vacuum that a radiation era beginning at time $\eta$ would select it has $\sinh r_k=1/(2k^2\eta^2)$. The second comparison squeezes twice as fast and is unitarily implementable; the first is not.

hep-th.title: The Skyrme-Dilaton and Nucleon Observables
hep-th.author: Thomas Fischbacher, Roman Zwicky
hep-th.abstract: We extend the Skyrme model by incorporating the $\sigma/f_0(500)$-meson as a dilaton. The motivation is twofold: the $\sigma$-meson is the lightest scalar resonance in QCD and is therefore the natural extensions to the pions of the classical Skyrme model, while its interpretation as a pseudo-Goldstone boson of spontaneously broken scale symmetry is supported by recent studies of gravitational form factors and related developments. Although the $\sigma$-meson is a broad resonance, for static observables it can be treated as real particle since its line-shape is not expected to be essential. A combined fit to static nucleon observables yields $\chi^2/\mathrm{dof} $ close to unity, with substantial improvement over the original Skyrme model, while simultaneously reproducing the physical value of $F_\pi$, the overall scale of the model.

hep-th.title: Axioms for relative entropy
hep-th.author: Roberto Longo
hep-th.abstract: For normal states of arbitrary von Neumann algebras, we characterize positive finite multiples of Araki relative entropy among non-degenerate divergences. The axioms are monotonicity under normal unital completely positive maps, tensor additivity, superadditivity for product second states, and separate lower semicontinuity in the predual norm. Alternatively, a conditional-expectation identity replaces the two tensor assumptions. The proof uses order bounds and asymptotic estimates on tensor powers. An appendix proves the known analytic estimates needed here, using standard modular theory and Haagerup L^p spaces. We also obtain the corresponding characterization in the C* algebraic setting.

hep-th.title: On the Asymptotic Expansion of Massive Fields in Spherically Symmetric Systems
hep-th.author: Robin Fynn Diedrichs, Iris van Gemeren
hep-th.abstract: The behavior of massive real scalar fields, when sourced by a central object, is usually assumed to follow a Yukawa falloff towards radial infinity. In this paper, we show that this is generically not the case, even for minimally coupled fields. Further, while the point-particle action provides a coordinate-invariant definition of the central object's scalar charge, we show that the coefficient one usually extracts at asymptotically large radii in the case of massive scalar fields is neither coordinate invariant nor identical to the scalar charge appearing in the point-particle action. We resolve this issue perturbatively by constructing matched asymptotic expansions and investigate the non-perturbative structure using numerical methods.

hep-th.title: Exceptional cubics on 7-manifolds
hep-th.author: Sergey Grigorian
hep-th.abstract: A $G_2$-structure $\varphi$ on a $7$-manifold $\mathcal M$ determines a two-dimensional space of invariant totally symmetric cubic forms on each fiber of the rank-$27$ bundle $S^2_0T^*\mathcal M$ of traceless symmetric $2$-tensors. This space is spanned by the trace cubic $C_0$ and a cubic $C_\varphi$ that, up to a constant factor, is the pointwise integrand of the Yukawa coupling on the $G_2$ moduli space. We determine the exact infinitesimal stabilizers over $\mathbb C$ of all nonzero cubics in this family. For $C_0+\lambda C_\varphi$, the stabilizer has dimension $78$ precisely at the two non-real values $\lambda_\pm=(1\pm i\sqrt7)/8$. Its dimension is $21$ for $C_0$ and $14$ in all other cases. At $\lambda_\pm$, the stabilizer is simple of type $E_6$, and the corresponding cubic is linearly equivalent to the complex Albert algebra cubic norm.The two cubics at $\lambda_\pm$, which we call critical, define complex-conjugate $E_6$-reductions of the complexified bundle. At any element with nonzero critical norm, the corresponding cubic determines a complex Albert algebra with basepoint stabilizer $F_4$; a line subbundle of the tangent bundle selects a smooth bundle of these algebras with tensorial operations and a Euclidean real form. The induced Levi-Civita connection preserves either critical cubic exactly when the $G_2$-structure is torsion-free. Its orthogonal projections onto the two exceptional reductions coincide with the connection induced by the minimal $G_2$-connection.

hep-th.title: A separation criterion for chiral systems and its application to Plebański--Demiański perturbations
hep-th.author: Hideo Furugori, Daisuke Yoshida
hep-th.abstract: We give a constructive criterion for local separation of first-order chiral systems coupling two complex doublets. It combines a Gram decomposition of the coupling sources with separate coordinate dependence and a differential transport test. For recoverable, nondegenerate source families, the criterion is necessary and sufficient within the specified class of mode-independent complex matrix transformations with unit determinant. For a fixed differential operator and admissible Gram decomposition, we identify conditions under which the sources uniquely determine the Hermitian coefficient matrix required for separation. As an application, we construct an explicit algebraic transformation and derive separated radial and angular equations for coupled radiative Einstein--Maxwell perturbations of rotating, charged Plebański--Demiański backgrounds with acceleration, NUT charge, and a cosmological constant, on specified local patches. Its Gram decomposition is unique under additional generic assumptions. We also derive angular endpoint indices for Bonnor and Misner identifications with conical deficits or excesses. Under the stated regularity assumptions, each specified self-adjoint angular realization at fixed real mode parameters has a discrete spectrum and a complete orthonormal eigenbasis.

hep-th.title: Boundary to bound dictionary for generic Kerr orbits
hep-th.author: Riccardo Gonzo, Canxin Shi
hep-th.abstract: We establish a new relation between classical observables for scattering and bound orbits of a massive probe particle in a Kerr background. We find an exact representation of the Hamilton-Jacobi action in terms of the conserved charges which admits an analytic continuation, both for the radial and polar contribution, for a general class of geodesics beyond the equatorial case. Remarkably, this allows to extend the boundary to bound dictionary and it provides an efficient method to compute the deflection angles and the time delay for scattering orbits, as well as frequency ratios for bound orbits, in the probe limit but at all orders in the perturbative expansion.

hep-th.title: Black Hole Chemistry Knows Extra Dimensions
hep-th.author: Kyung Kiu Kim, Jeongwon Ho, Seungjoon Hyun, Taehyeon Song
hep-th.abstract: We study black hole chemistry in the eight-dimensional Einstein-Yang-Mills-Maxwell theory, where the stabilized size of the compact internal space dynamically determines the four-dimensional thermodynamic pressure. Analyzing AdS black holes, we show that larger extra dimensions lower phase-transition temperatures and broaden the range of thermodynamically excluded black hole sizes. Additionally, we investigate a geometric representation of the thermodynamic volume by defining a volume-constrained minimal surface using a lapse-weighted volume functional. This codimension-two surface minimizes its area under the constraint that its enclosed volume exactly matches the thermodynamic volume. This surface prescription naturally reproduces the event horizon for dyonic and Schwarzschild-AdS black holes. We also apply this to the Kerr--AdS black hole and find an off-horizon surface numerically and analytically for finite and small angular momenta. In addition, we interpret the thermodynamic volume in terms of an effective number of disentanglers in a MERA system.

hep-th.title: Entropic force in matrix theory
hep-th.author: Wei-shui Xu
hep-th.abstract: We consider the entropic force in matrix theory. We find the gravity in bulk can be emergent from the entropic force.

hep-th.title: Higher genus twistor spaces and the celestial torus
hep-th.author: Seraphim Jarov
hep-th.abstract: This paper studies novel four-dimensional integrable field theories that are deformations of self-dual Yang-Mills. They are engineered by considering holomorphic Chern-Simons and BF type theories on covers of twistor space obtained by pulling back the vector bundle $\mathcal{O}(1)^2\to\mathbb{CP}^1$ to hyperelliptic or elliptic curves. Compactifying to 4d yields an integrable theory, which in the examples I study, are determined to leading order. The form of the higher-order corrections are bootstrapped, and I argue that the index structure and coefficients of these terms are fixed by integrability. The celestial chiral algebras of these theories are shown to live on hyper-elliptic and elliptic curves, respectively. Symmetry reducing these integrable deformations to 2d yields an example of a hyperelliptic and elliptic integrable model governing a deformation of Hitchin's equations.

hep-th.title: Hamiltonian Truncation Framework for Gauge Theories on the Interval
hep-th.author: Rachel Houtz, James Ingoldby
hep-th.abstract: In this work, we investigate gauge theories in two dimensions nonperturbatively using the Hamiltonian truncation approach. Working on a spatial interval and adopting the axial gauge, we remove all gauge field degrees of freedom and express the interacting Hamiltonian in the eigenbasis of the free Dirac theory, truncated at a finite energy. As a benchmark we analyse the Schwinger model, where our numerical spectra agree closely with the exact results from bosonization across a wide range of couplings, validating the construction of the Hamiltonian. We then generalize the formulation to nonabelian gauge groups and apply it to SU(3) gauge theory with a single massless Dirac fermion. These results demonstrate that gauge theories can be explored nonperturbatively using a truncated Hamiltonian that generates evolutions in ordinary time, offering a complementary alternative to lattice field theory.

hep-th.title: A geometrical invitation to BMS group theory
hep-th.author: Xavier Bekaert, Yannick Herfray, Lea Mele, Noémie Parrini
hep-th.abstract: In these lecture notes, a group-theoretical introduction to BMS symmetries is provided in a self-contained manner. More precisely, all definitions and structures are purely based on geometrical and group-theoretical notions defined at null infinity and valid in any dimension (four or higher), in a way that circumvents its traditional bulk realisation as asymptotic symmetries. The topics which are reviewed are: the definition of BMS transformations as conformal Carrollian isometries of null infinity, the semidirect structure of the BMS group, the holographic reconstruction of Minkowski spacetime in terms of good cuts, the one-to-one correspondence between good cut subspaces and Poincaré subgroups (aka vacua), as well as a basic introduction to the unitary representations of the BMS group.

hep-th.title: BPS vortex from nonpolynomial scalar QED in a $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^1$-Maxwell theory
hep-th.author: F. C. E. Lima
hep-th.abstract: We investigate a generalized gauged $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^1$-Maxwell theory in which the electromagnetic sector acquires a field-dependent magnetic permeability generated dynamically through fermionic vacuum polarization. We couple a Dirac fermion with an effective mass to a gauged $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^1$ sigma model whose target space carries the Fubini-Study metric. Integrating out the Dirac fermion at one loop induces a logarithmic correction to the Maxwell kinetic term. This dependence is retained in the planar effective theory after dimensional reduction. Within this framework, one builds a generalized $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{P}^1$-Maxwell model by admitting Bogomol'nyi-Prasad-Sommerfield (BPS) configurations. Taking this into account, we solved the self-dual equations that describe vortex-like solutions with quantized magnetic flux.

hep-th.title: Conformal Vacua in Boundary-Glued AdS$_3$
hep-th.author: Lucas K. Kovalsky, Shivesh Pathak, Kyle Ritchie
hep-th.abstract: We argue that the purely topological gluing of AdS$_3$ spacetimes, which are otherwise independent due to Dirichlet boundary conditions, can still produce non-trivial spaces after a quotient. In this direction, we extend the study of a recently discovered non-orientable AdS$_3$, which is a $\mathbb Z_2$ quotient of two AdS$_3$ spaces glued along their conformal boundaries. We find that this space is compact and boundaryless and that the quotient sends the gluing surface to a torus comprised of a null lattice with halved periods. However, the bulk wraps around both its sides, which means that as an embedded space this gluing surface forms a one-sided torus. We discover that it supports a permutation-twisted sector of two CFT$_2$s with shared Dirichlet boundary conditions and conjecture that conformal maps can be extended across this gluing surface. Using this extension, we show that the vacuum of pairs of Rindler wedges, which share a boundary in this non-orientable AdS$_3\times$S$^2$ space, are conformal to static patch vacua, which are supported on two dS$_4\times \mathbb R$ glued together at their conformal boundaries.

hep-th.title: Effective Field Theory for Superconducting Phase Transitions
hep-th.author: Yanyan Bu, Zexin Yang
hep-th.abstract: Employing the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, we formulate an effective field theory for s-wave superconducting phase transition, where the dynamical variables consist of electromagnetic gauge field and complex scalar order parameter. Symmetry-constrained effective action allows systematic handling of dissipations and fluctuations. In particular, we explore the physical implications of higher-order terms, including those involving additional dynamical fields as well as higher time derivatives, on the real-time dynamics near the superconducting critical point. When appropriately truncated, the effective field theory reproduces the phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau equations. Upon crossing the critical temperature into the low-temperature phase, the electromagnetic gauge symmetry undergoes spontaneous breaking induced by the condensate of the order parameter. Collective excitation analysis reveals that the Higgs mode behaves as an overdamped diffusive mode near the critical point, while the phase fluctuation is absorbed into the gauge field via the Higgs mechanism. For complex kinetic coefficients, we derive the coupled linearized equations for amplitude, phase, and longitudinal gauge fluctuations, and distinguish propagation from damping through their complex poles. The holographic Schwinger-Keldysh construction provides an explicit realization and a nontrivial consistency check of the effective action, and determines its Wilsonian coefficients within a specific strongly coupled model. Holographic results reveal a complex relaxation parameter that indicates oscillatory dynamics characteristic of strongly coupled systems.

hep-th.title: Entanglement inequalities for timelike intervals within dynamical holography
hep-th.author: Gaurav Katoch, Debajyoti Sarkar, Bhim Sen
hep-th.abstract: This paper extends our previous work (arXiv:2504.14313) of a single timelike subregion to two, in the framework of AdS$_3$-Vaidya holography. We confirm the positivity of timelike mutual information and the statement of weak monotonicity when the subregions are non-overlapping. We also study entanglement inequalities such as Araki-Lieb inequality and strong subadditivity when the intervals start to overlap. In line with the recent findings in the literature, we provide explicit working examples showing that the timelike version of the strong subadditivity is generally violated in these setups, even though the statements of subadditivity and Araki-Lieb inequality hold true.

hep-th.title: A gravity interpretation for the complex saddles of the ABJM and spindle indices
hep-th.author: Minwoo Suh
hep-th.abstract: The superconformal index is a grand-canonical partition function that counts the 1/16-BPS states in the theory, and its Legendre transform with respect to reduced chemical potentials accounts for the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of electrically charged rotating black holes in anti-de Sitter spacetime. However, the superconformal index of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory appears to allow shifts in chemical potentials, and the contributions of the shifted terms diverge exponentially. We resolved this puzzle by showing the instability of wrapped D3-branes corresponding to shifts in the gravitational on-shell action. Analogously, we study the M5-brane instability criterion of the ABJM index and the spindle index.

hep-th.title: Filtering out Erratic Observables: Wormholes from Gauging Nonlocal Symmetries
hep-th.author: Qi-Feng Wu
hep-th.abstract: The wormhole contribution to the gravitational path integral may be interpreted as smooth remnant of correlations among the erratic large-$N$ behaviors of dual CFTs. In this work, we investigate this idea in (2+1)-dimensional gravity. We show that one-sided boundary gravitons are intrinsically incomplete in the sense that the associated observable algebra has a nontrivial center regardless of choices of boundary conditions. Based on asymptotic symmetries, we bootstrap a general Poisson bracket to construct completions of the boundary gravitons. In the simplest completion, the commutant of the boundary graviton observable algebra is given by an observable algebra of monodromy data which we interpret as an effective description of one-sided black holes. We show that, to describe Lorentzian multi-boundary wormholes, only the monodromy data with a positivity restriction is needed. The positivity restriction results in emergent erratic large-$N$ behaviors for some observables. We filter out the erratic observables by restricting to a subspace on which they act trivially. The monodromy observables generate nonlocal symmetries lack of corresponding local currents. We show that gauging the nonlocal symmetries is equivalent to filtering out the erratic observables. For one CFT, gauging the nonlocal symmetries at the quantum level removes all black hole states. Filtering the partition function of CFTs leads to an apparent ensemble averaging. For two CFTs, a Hilbert subspace describing wormholes survives after gauging global part of the nonlocal symmetries. The filtered partition function of the two CFTs is an ensemble average over quantum gates entangling the monodromy degrees of freedom of the two CFTs. The correlation between the erratic observables of the two CFTs is preserved, which contributes to the filtered partition function as a wormhole term.

hep-th.title: Stress Tensor Deformations in dS/CFT: Mixed Boundary Conditions, Spectrum Flow and Pseudo Entropy
hep-th.author: Feng Hao, Hao Ouyang, Xi-Yang Ran
hep-th.abstract: We formulate a local semiclassical source--response prescription for derivative-free stress-tensor deformations in dS/CFT. The metric flow determines the deformed boundary metric and stress tensor, encoding the deformation through mixed boundary conditions at future infinity. In Kerr-dS$_3$/CFT$_2$, the holographic charges reproduce the field-theory spectral flow, providing an internal consistency check. For general deformations in this class, we derive a holographic pseudo-entropy formula in terms of the flowed boundary data, nonperturbative in the deformation parameters within a specified complex-geodesic prescription. We evaluate this formula explicitly for the $T\bar{T}$ and root-$T\bar{T}$ deformations. On the non-rotating principal branch, an analytically continued replica calculation reproduces the interval-dependent corrections at first order in the couplings and leading semiclassical order. Agreement of the interval-independent terms additionally requires a source-frame regulator identification.

hep-th.title: O(N) BCFT: new data from conformal partial wave expansions
hep-th.author: Jozef Csipes, Petr Vaško
hep-th.abstract: The $\mathsf{O}(N)$ $\mathsf{BCFT}$ is analyzed in the large $N$ expansion in a generic bulk dimension $2<d+1<4$. Focus is on boundary conditions corresponding to the ordinary transition, however techniques used can be generalized to special or extraordinary transitions. We study the system of bulk $2$-pt functions $\langle \phi\phi\rangle$, $\langle \phi^2 \phi^2\rangle$ and $\langle \sigma\sigma \rangle$, where $\sigma$ is the Hubbard--Stratonovich field. They are expanded in bulk/boundary conformal partial waves. The coefficient functions of this expansion -- the spectral functions -- encode $\mathsf{BCFT}$ data and determine bulk/boundary conformal block expansions. We prove conjectures about boundary spectral functions in Dujava et al. [arXiv:2503.16345] and reproduce the bulk expansion of $\langle \phi\phi \rangle$ in Giombi et al. [arXiv:2007.04955]. The bulk expansion of $\langle\sigma\sigma\rangle$ is new and allows to extract the leading large $N$ expression for an unknown OPE coefficient $C_{\sigma\sigma\sigma^3}$ (the computation outputs as a byproduct also a mixing coefficient, which matches an existing result by Derkachov et al. [arXiv:hep-th/9705020], providing further support for the main result). Besides these derived data infinitely many constraints are produced, though due to operator mixing growing in complexity as degeneracy increases, they cannot be disentangled without further input.

hep-th.title: On the Schubert calculus of the quantum K-theory for partial flag manifolds: a 3d A-model perspective
hep-th.author: Zhihao Duan, Osama Khlaif, Hao Zou
hep-th.abstract: We further investigate the 3d gauged linear sigma model (GLSM)/~quantum K-theory correspondence for partial flag manifolds $X \equiv {\rm Fl}(\boldsymbol{k};n)$. This is a 3d uplift of the 2d GLSM/quantum cohomology correspondence with the 3d theory compactified on $\mathbb{R}^2\times S^1_\beta$. Recently, a set of half-BPS line operators, called Schubert line defects, were constructed that correspond to the Schubert classes in the K-theory ring of $X$. Utilizing algebro-geometric algorithms, we compute $2$-point and $3$-point correlation functions of these line operators in the 3d A-model regime of the theory. These are interpreted as genus-$0$ K-theoretic Gromov--Witten invariants, and they produce the K-theoretic Littlewood--Richardson coefficients of the quantum K-theory ring of $X$. We show how this works explicitly in examples, going beyond the existing results in the literature. Taking the small $\beta$ limit, we apply these techniques to the resulting 2d GLSM. We explicitly compute the quantum cohomology ring relations of $X$ for some cases and match with existing results in the literature in examples.

hep-th.title: Diagonally gauged anomaly-free 6D supergravities and their vacua
hep-th.author: Xu Guo, Yi Pang, Henning Samtleben, Ergin Sezgin
hep-th.abstract: We study anomaly-free six-dimensional $N=(1,0)$ supergravities with $n_T=1$ and diagonal $U(1)_{R+}$ or $Sp(1)_{R+}$ gauging. The diagonal group combines R-symmetry with a commuting action on hypermultiplets. We perform bounded searches for anomaly-free models with one or two additional simple gauge group factors of rank at most 30, impose string-charge lattice and positive kinetic term conditions, and tabulate the resulting spectra. The main scans cover $q_{\max}\leq2$ and $d_{\max}\leq3$, where $q_{\max}$ is the largest absolute hyperino charge and $d_{\max}$ the largest diagonal $Sp(1)$ representation dimension, with supplementary searches at larger values. Every hypermultiplet block is required to be nontrivial under at least one additional simple gauge factor. The search has led to a large number of models. Here we give the details of 93 models with $G_+= U(1)_{R+}$ and $q_{\rm max}\le 2$, and 26 models with $G_+=Sp(1)_{R+}$ and $d_{\rm max}\le 3$, and one or two simple group factors. Additional 1341 and 494 models with $G_+=U(1)_{R+}$ with $q_{\rm max}=2$ and $Sp(1)_{R+}$ with $d_{\rm max}=3$, respectively, are posted to the GitHub repository. We establish the existence of supersymmetric Minkowski vacua for all the anomaly free models we have found with $q_{\rm max}=2$ and $d_{\rm max}=3$. We find that such vacua require $q_{\max}>1$ for $U(1)_{R+}$, and $d_{\max}>2$ for $Sp(1)_{R+}$. We also show that every Minkowski vacuum breaks R-symmetry, with the connected unbroken gauge group contained in the additional gauge factors. At two-derivative order, while our anomaly free models do not admit AdS$_6$ solutions, all those with $q_{\rm max} = 2$ and $d_{\rm max}=3$ have non-supersymmetric and unstable dS$_6$ vacua as well.

hep-th.title: Interacting Galilean and Finite-Energy Carroll Fermions
hep-th.author: Pulastya Parekh, Aditya Sharma, Mauricio Valenzuela
hep-th.abstract: We develop a common similarity-transformation framework for Galilean and Carrollian Dirac contractions, encompassing Lévy--Leblond and magnetic Carroll spin-half systems. Explicit field maps relate free formulations with different mass and energy parametrizations. We obtain the complete five-parameter family of derivative-free Hermitian quartic potentials for a pair of Grassmann-odd Pauli spinors, invariant under rotations, a common $U(1)$, and triangular boosts. Higher-order and color-mixed interactions admit exact classical solutions. An independent pairing channel generates derivative interactions upon exact auxiliary elimination and sources otherwise absent Carroll spinor components. Quartic deformations of a Galilean fermionic gauge theory yield algebraic or spatial differential equations while preserving a local phase symmetry. Nambu--Jona-Lasinio contractions provide relativistic origins for selected channels.

hep-th.title: Heterotic string couplings at order $α'^3$ in NS-NS sector
hep-th.author: Alireza Pahlavan, Mehdi Ameri, Mohammad R. Garousi
hep-th.abstract: We utilize the standard T-duality procedure to derive the classical effective action of heterotic string theory at the eight-derivative order within the NS-NS sector, which comprises the metric, the \(B\)-field, and the dilaton. Starting from the minimal basis at this order, consisting of 872 even-parity and 477 odd-parity couplings, we perform a dimensional reduction on a circle and impose invariance under T-duality transformations, specifically the Buscher rules supplemented by higher-derivative corrections. This invariance uniquely fixes a subset of the couplings to match those of type II theory up to an overall factor, while the remaining couplings are determined in terms of the coefficients at order \(\alpha'\). For these latter couplings, we adopt both the Metsaev-Tseytlin and Meissner schemes. Subsequently, through field redefinitions, we recast the action into a canonical form in which the dilaton appears solely through the overall factor \(e^{-2\Phi}\). In the Meissner scheme, the pure gravity sector precisely reproduces the known S-matrix results. In both schemes, the pure gravity terms can be expressed as the double trace \((\Tr(R^2))^2\), and when combined with the corresponding Yang-Mills terms \((\Tr(F^2))^2\), they take the unified form \((\Tr(R^2-F^2))^2\), as anticipated in the literature.

hep-th.title: Entanglement Harvesting Landscapes: A Common Computational Framework
hep-th.author: Rahul Nigam, Ujjwala Vadrevu, Akshay Kulkarni
hep-th.abstract: Entanglement harvesting provides an operational means of probing nonlocal correlations of quantum fields through localized detector-field interactions. Although studied in diverse spacetime backgrounds and quantum field states, existing studies largely focus on individual detector configurations. Here, we develop a unified perturbative framework for localized Unruh-DeWitt detectors, applicable to different detector trajectories and quantum field states through the corresponding Wightman function. Expressing detector responses in dimensionless variables and analytically reducing the perturbative integrals to numerically efficient representations enables systematic exploration of multidimensional harvesting landscapes and phase boundaries. We investigate inertial detectors in the Minkowski vacuum, thermal field states, and uniformly accelerated detectors undergoing Born-rigid motion. In the latter case, the detectors have different proper accelerations and different Unruh temperatures, leading to unequal local excitation probabilities. The harvested entanglement is evaluated by accounting for both local detector responses and the nonlocal exchange amplitude. Increasing temperature enhances the detector excitation probability while generally suppressing the magnitude of the nonlocal exchange amplitude. Consequently, within the perturbative Gaussian-switching framework and over the parameter range investigated, thermal effects suppress harvested entanglement and reduce the spatial extent of the harvesting region. The resulting landscapes provide a global characterization of detector-field interactions and demonstrate how temperature and observer motion reshape the competition between local detector noise and nonlocal field correlations. This framework provides an extensible methodology for investigating entanglement harvesting across relativistic quantum systems.

hep-th.title: Stringy Gauge Structures
hep-th.author: Gerardo Aldazabal, Eduardo C. Andrés, Lucía M. Cabrera, Martín Mayo
hep-th.abstract: A field theory action, able to incorporate stringy gauge symmetry enhancement-breaking effects, which occur at particular points of moduli space in a heterotic string toroidal compactification framework, was previously constructed from three-point interactions and duality symmetries. Via doubled periodic coordinates and a non-commutative product, it encodes the non-Abelian structure in a background-independent form. Moduli-space dependence becomes manifest upon performing a generalized mode expansion. Here we further elaborate on this construction. In particular, we propose field transformations for the retained sectors that make up the foundations of a potential symmetry of the action and that, when mode expanded at enhancement points in moduli space, contain the usual non-Abelian gauge transformations. We also examine the covariance of the corresponding scalar derivative structures. Although the proposal must be regarded as a truncated version of a full, presently unknown field-theory description, it already encodes representations of massless and massive states containing up to one oscillator excitation. Finally, we relate the construction to gauged DFT with an extended tangent space by associating generalized Kaluza-Klein modes considered here with additional generalized-frame directions. At enhancement, their brackets reproduce the enhanced gauge algebra; away from enhancement, the same algebraic structure is recovered by rotating the Cartan basis.

hep-th.title: Differential equations for Dotsenko--Fateev integrals: the case of degenerate fields $Φ_{n,1}$
hep-th.author: Aleksandra Ivanova
hep-th.abstract: We study higher-order differential equations corresponding to integrals of the Dotsenko--Fateev type and associated with four-point correlation functions with degenerate fields $\Phi_{n,1}$. We determine the general structure and coefficients of the equations in terms of the integral parameters $ \{ A,B,C,g \} $. In particular, special cases of these equations in CFT are used for verification. In addition, the relationship between higher-order differential equations and hypergeometric operators is established.

hep-th.title: Quantum vacuum inversion and multi-kink unbinding in the non-degenerate double sine-Gordon model
hep-th.author: Jonathan Lozano-Mayo
hep-th.abstract: Quantum fluctuations can unbind a composite soliton while the correction to its mass stays small. We show this beyond perturbation theory for the multi-kinks of the non-degenerate double sine-Gordon model. At one loop the vacuum at the centre of the multi-kink becomes the true vacuum at a coupling of order the classical lifting of the vacua. Tensor-network calculations of the lattice theory show that this inversion survives beyond one loop and has a continuum limit, and that the Gaussian effective potential captures it. On finite chains the multi-kink unbinds when the tension of the string of central vacuum between its two halves falls through zero

hep-th.title: Reduction technique for expanding the Feynman diagrams in AdS$_2$
hep-th.author: V.S. Khiteev
hep-th.abstract: We formulate the reduction technique for expanding the $n$-point AdS Feynman diagrams in two dimensions into the Wilson line networks. The technique applies to any $n$-point tree diagram, expressing it as several series of the matrix elements of Wilson line network operators, and employs the Wilson network expansions of the $(n-1)$-point AdS$_2$ Feynman diagrams, which can in turn be obtained using the same technique. Consequently, the complexity of this technique does not increase with $n$, provided that the expansions of the $(n-1)$-point diagrams are known. To demonstrate the reduction technique, we apply it to all topologically distinct five-point AdS$_2$ Feynman tree diagrams. The resulting expansions near the conformal boundary reproduce the known decompositions of the corresponding five-point Witten diagrams into conformal blocks.

hep-th.title: From Critical Zero Modes to Interior Dynamics in Holographic Superconductors
hep-th.author: Yan Liu, Hong-Da Lyu
hep-th.abstract: We study how the critical behavior of holographic superconductors controls the interior geometry of charged black holes. Although the exterior condensate vanishes at criticality, the critical zero mode develops logarithmic oscillations near the Reissner--Nordström Cauchy horizon, rendering the interior critical limit nonuniform. We show that the transmitted critical-mode amplitude, together with local Cauchy-horizon quantities, fixes both the leading Einstein--Rosen collapse $\Delta z_{\rm ER}$ width and the phase $\Theta_J$ in the subsequent Josephson regime. If the condensate obeys $t\equiv1-T/T_c\propto\epsilon^{2r}$, then $\Delta z_{\rm ER}\propto t^{1/r}$ and $\Theta_J\propto t^{-1/r}$. This Josephson phase is transferred to the first Kasner epoch, producing oscillatory Kasner exponents and an accumulation law $t_n\sim n^{-r}$ for successive zeros of the scalar velocity. The critical zero mode fixes the leading collapse and phase coefficients, which are quantitatively confirmed by fully nonlinear solutions in both the ordinary and tricritical cases. At low temperature, the interior instead depends on the infrared completion of the zero-temperature geometry. Thus near-critical scaling is governed by critical-mode transmission, whereas the low-temperature behavior is controlled by the infrared endpoint.

hep-th.title: Holographic two-point functions across a PT symmetry-breaking transition
hep-th.author: Zuo Wang, Liang He
hep-th.abstract: In parity-time (PT)-symmetric non-Hermitian systems, an exceptional point, where eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce, typically separates a real spectrum from complex-conjugate eigenvalues. In logarithmic conformal field theories (LCFTs), such an exceptional point appears in the spectrum of scaling dimensions. Holographic models of LCFTs, such as the dipole model, are built exactly at this point. Here, we deform the holographic dipole model so that its two coalescing scaling dimensions split into either two real ones or a complex-conjugate pair. We obtain the renormalized two-point functions in closed form. They change continuously from a linear combination of two power laws, through the logarithmic form of the LCFT at the exceptional point, to log-periodic oscillations. For any pair of scalar primary operators with real mixing under dilatations, the conformal Ward identities fix this form up to two normalization constants, which the holographic dictionary determines. In PT-symmetric theories with such a dilatation operator, real and complex-conjugate scaling dimensions correspond to the PT-unbroken and PT-broken phases. In the BTZ black hole at finite temperature, the difference between the quasinormal frequencies associated with the two scaling dimensions changes from purely imaginary to purely real across the real-to-complex spectral transition. Correspondingly, the linear response changes from overdamped to underdamped, with critical damping at the exceptional point. Direct experimental observation of the two-point functions across the exceptional point could be achieved in two hyperbolic electric circuits with a non-reciprocal coupling, through the voltage response between their edge nodes.

hep-th.title: Reconstructing Meson Parton Distributions from Mellin Moments with Artificial Neural Networks
hep-th.author: Pietro Dall'Olio, Cristian Del Gobbo, Khépani Raya, José Rodríguez-Quintero
hep-th.abstract: We address the inverse problem of reconstructing a meson parton distribution function (PDF) or parton distribution amplitude (PDA) at a fixed scale from a finite set of Mellin moments. At finite moment order this map is ill posed in the Hadamard sense: the moments do not determine a unique, stable pointwise $x$-dependence, and small data perturbations can produce large changes in the reconstruction. We regularize the problem by restricting the admissible function class through constraints justified by first principles---support on $x\in[0,1]$, endpoint vanishing, unit normalization, and, for the pion, the exact $x\leftrightarrow 1-x$ symmetry---and by complementing these hard constraints with differentiable penalties that suppress the spurious multiple maxima and central concavity changes typical of ill-posed inversions. We parameterize the unknown function with two interchangeable neural cores, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) and a Kolmogorov--Arnold network (KAN), and find that the KAN reconstructs the target distributions more accurately, most markedly in the asymmetric (kaon) case. We attribute this advantage to the locality of the B-spline basis underlying the KAN, which localizes corrections during moment matching and damps the global oscillations to which the MLP is prone. Benchmarks against synthetic targets, using both ten and five input moments, support these conclusions.

hep-th.title: Holographic dual of the 2d Ising model
hep-th.author: Kazumi Okuyama
hep-th.abstract: We propose a holographic dual of the 2d Ising model on a torus as the Turaev-Viro TQFT on a solid torus. The bulk spacetime is divided into the ``core'' region and the ``sandwich'' region. The core region prepares a defect state $|\mathcal{D}\rangle$ on the topological boundary $\mathbb{D}$. The sandwich region computes the Turaev-Viro state sum $\langle\mathcal{D}|\Pi|\mathcal{F}\rangle$ between the state $|\mathcal{D}\rangle$ on $\mathbb{D}$ and the state $|\mathcal{F}\rangle$ on the physical boundary $\mathbb{B}$. The fusion diagram (or string-net) $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbb{B}$ is given by the Aasen-Fendley-Mong construction. There is also a ``bedding surface'' $\mathbb{S}$ between $\mathbb{D}$ and $\mathbb{B}$, and the height variables (or Ising spins inside/outside of the domain wall) are naturally living on $\mathbb{S}$. The bulk spacetime is discretized by the 2-skeleton $P$ which interpolates $\mathcal{D}$ and $\mathcal{F}$. When the defect $\mathcal{D}$ is absent, the 2-skeleton $P$ ends on the bedding surface $\mathbb{S}$ and $P$ is interpreted as the bulk worldsheet of the string-net $\mathcal{F}$.

hep-th.title: Bound States of Two D0-Branes and the Three-Graviton Coupling
hep-th.author: Sergio Sanjurjo, Themistocles Zikopoulos
hep-th.abstract: We numerically solve for the ground state of the $SU(2)$ BFSS matrix model for M-theory. This state corresponds to the zero-energy bound state of two D0-branes or, by the BFSS conjecture, to the eleven-dimensional graviton with two units of momentum along the M-theory circle. The wavefunction exhibits a strongly coupled core, as well as an asymptotic power-law tail where the D0-branes are well separated. The coefficient of this power-law decay is the three-graviton coupling, previously computed by Herderschee and Maldacena, which our numerical solution reproduces with high accuracy. We also show that this coupling is protected by supersymmetry in the matrix model, and derive its value from the non-renormalized one-loop interaction of the two D0-branes. Lastly, we provide a simple representation-theoretic argument regarding the recently proposed excited bound states of the model.

hep-th.title: A Breakdown Case Study of the Lindblad Approach via Entanglement and Purity
hep-th.author: Raoul Serao, Aniello Quaranta, Antonio Capolupo, Fabio Franchini, Salvatore Marco Giampaolo
hep-th.abstract: The Lindblad master equation is widely used to describe the reduced dynamics of open quantum systems under Markovian assumptions. Here, we investigate its ability to reproduce the reduced evolution emerging from a microscopic many-body model in which two interacting two-level subsystems are embedded in a larger environment and evolve under fully unitary dynamics. The exact evolution exhibits a clear separation of timescales. At short times, decoherence arises from environmentally induced dephasing, leading to a Gaussian suppression of coherences and a quadratic decay of purity. At intermediate times, collective decoherence channels saturate and a slower, still Gaussian, decay driven by relative environmental fluctuations dominates. At later times the system settles in a complete decohered state. The first two behaviors cannot be reproduced by a Lindblad dynamics with constant coefficients, which always results in an exponential decay: Our work provides a simple example of the breakdown of the effective description relevant in many realistic settings.

hep-th.title: The symplectic geometry of the black hole photon shell
hep-th.author: Judy Shir, Shahar Hadar
hep-th.abstract: The unstably bound, critical null geodesics of the Kerr spacetime form a distinguished class of orbits whose properties govern observables such as the photon ring and the high-frequency component of black-hole ringdown. This set of orbits defines a codimension-two submanifold of the null-geodesic phase space known as the photon shell. In this work we investigate the photon shell's intrinsic symplectic geometry. Using the induced symplectic form, we construct the canonical volume form on the shell and compute the differential phase-space volume it encloses as a function of radius -- equivalently, the radial density of states. In the near-extremal limit the photon shell bifurcates into near-horizon and far-region components; we find that approximately $3\%$ of the shell's phase-space volume resides in the near-horizon component. We also analyze a thickening of the photon shell that includes near-critical orbits, and compute its differential phase-space volume. Beyond their intrinsic theoretical interest, these results may inform the interpretation of high-resolution observations of spinning black holes.

hep-th.title: Non-Stationary Difference Equation and Affine Laumon Space III: Generalization to $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$
hep-th.author: Hidetoshi Awata, Koji Hasegawa, Hiroaki Kanno, Ryo Ohkawa, Shamil Shakirov, Jun'ichi Shiraishi, Yasuhiko Yamada
hep-th.abstract: In a series of papers, we have considered a non-stationary difference equation which was originally discovered for the deformed Virasoro conformal block. The equation involves mass parameters and, when they are tuned appropriately, the equation is regarded as a quantum KZ equation for $U_q\bigl(A_{1}^{(1)}\bigr)$. We introduce a $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ generalization of the non-stationary difference equation. The Hamiltonian is expressed in terms of $q$-commuting variables and allows both factorized forms and a normal ordered form. By specializing the mass parameters appropriately, the Hamiltonian can be identified with the $R$-matrix of the symmetric tensor representation of $U_q\bigl(A_{N-1}^{(1)}\bigr)$, which in turn comes from the 3D (tetrahedron) $R$-matrix. We conjecture that the affine Laumon partition function of type $A_{N-1}^{(1)}$ gives a solution to our $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ non-stationary difference equation. As a check of our conjecture, we work out the four-dimensional limit and find that the non-stationary difference equation reduces to the Fuji-Suzuki-Tsuda system.

hep-th.title: A Quantum Many-Body Approach for Orbital Magnetism in Correlated Multiband Electron Systems
hep-th.author: Mengxing Ye
hep-th.abstract: Orbital magnetism is a purely quantum phenomenon that reflects intrinsic electronic properties of solids, yet its microscopic description in interacting multiband systems remains incomplete. We develop a general quantum many-body framework for orbital magnetic responses based on the Luttinger--Ward functional. Starting from the Dyson equation, we reformulate the thermodynamic potential in a weak magnetic field and construct a controlled expansion in powers of $B$ applicable to correlated electron systems. A key technical advance is a modified ``Fourier'' representation using noncommutative coordinates, which allows the thermodynamic potential to be expressed in an effective momentum space where the magnetic field acts perturbatively. This formulation makes analytic progress possible within the Moyal algebra. As an application, we derive the spontaneous orbital magnetization for approximations whose skeleton diagrams contain no fermion loop enclosing magnetic flux (e.g., Hartree--Fock, self-consistent RPA, and single-site dynamical mean-field theory). Vertex corrections consistent with the self-energy are included automatically, without a separate diagrammatic analysis, and the result is expressed entirely in terms of the zero-field Hamiltonian renormalized by the self-energy. For frequency-dependent but Hermitian self-energies, we generalize the orbital magnetic moment and Berry curvature to momentum-frequency space and identify two gauge-invariant contributions built from these quantities. For frequency-independent self-energies the result reduces to the familiar geometric formula for noninteracting systems. This framework provides a unified foundation for computing orbital magnetic responses in correlated multiband materials.

hep-th.title: Kinematic Foundations of Defect-Mediated Plasticity: A Gauge-Theoretic Framework
hep-th.author: Kevin T. Grosvenor, Mario Solís, Piotr Surówka
hep-th.abstract: Plastic deformation is widely regarded as an intrinsically dissipative phenomenon whose theoretical description relies heavily on phenomenological constitutive assumptions. We argue instead that defect-mediated plasticity possesses a universal, non-dissipative backbone: the kinematics and mobility constraints of defects are fixed by symmetry and conservation laws prior to dissipation. Starting from the spontaneous breaking of spacetime symmetries in a crystalline phase, we construct an effective field theory in which elasticity reorganizes into a coupled higher-rank tensor-vector gauge structure emerging directly from stress and defect conservation laws rather than being postulated microscopically. Dislocations, disclinations, and singular frame-geometric configurations appear as gauge sources whose coupled continuity equations and mobility constraints follow from generalized Gauss laws. The construction provides a symmetry-based organization of the kinematic sectors relevant to defect-mediated plasticity and a starting point for a subsequent dissipative theory of defect motion and stress relaxation.

hep-th.title: The $\mathbb{Z}_N^{\times 3}$ symmetry protected boundary modes in two-dimensional Potts paramagnets
hep-th.author: Hrant Topchyan
hep-th.abstract: We construct and analyze a class of one-dimensional boundary Hamiltonians arising from two-dimensional symmetry-protected topological phases with $\mathbb{Z}_N^{\times 3}$ symmetry on a triangular lattice. Using a cohomology-based transformation, the lattice models for the edge modes are explicitly obtained, and their structure is shown to be governed by the arithmetic properties of $N$. For prime $N$, the boundary theory admits a formulation in terms of mutually commuting Temperley-Lieb algebras. For the composite values of $N$, the models exhibit hierarchical or factorized structures. We demonstrate that the phases can be understood in terms of primary models augmented by local defect degrees of freedom that partition the system into independent segments. Finally, the global symmetry is realized on the boundary in a non-on-site and anomalous manner, directly realizing the corresponding 't Hooft anomaly.

hep-th.title: Exact SU(2) Yang-Mills Waves from a Simple Ansatz
hep-th.author: Yu-Xuan Zhang, Jing-Ling Chen
hep-th.abstract: We use an ansatz based on rotations of the Pauli basis to construct exact propagating solutions of the sourceless SU(2) Yang--Mills equations in $(3+1)$ dimensions. By examining and extending this ansatz, we obtain two wave families with nontrivial transverse structures and a family of finite-amplitude waves on a self-similar non-Abelian background. These solutions can retain a genuinely non-Abelian structure while admitting arbitrary wave profiles propagating at the speed of light and carrying the corresponding longitudinal electric or magnetic fields. We also investigate the parameter conditions for their non-Abelian character and their energy transport. For the self-similar family, we study the structure of its singular plane and construct suitable sources to replace the singular region while preserving wave propagation in the remaining regions. This offers a possible interpretation of these solutions as propagating fields outside sources.

hep-th.title: Probing String-Theory-Inspired Topologies of the Early Universe through CMB Temperature and Polarization Anisotropies
hep-th.author: Nick E. Mavromatos, Miguel-Angel Sanchis-Lozano
hep-th.abstract: TeV string-mass-scale strings have been excluded experimentally at colliders, as their effects have not been observed at the Large Hadron Collider (CERN). On the other hand, higher-scale string theory, with mass scales typically close to the Planck scale, is often regarded as experimentally inaccessible due to the enormous energies required for direct tests, and far beyond the reach of present or foreseeable particle accelerators. Nevertheless, the early Universe may provide an indirect observational window for high-string scale through imprints left on the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB). In this work, building on previous studies, we reexamine temperature and polarization angular correlations as probes of the geometry and topology of the pre-inflationary Universe. We focus in particular on two-point correlation functions at large angular scales, where signatures of nontrivial spatial topology may survive as relics of primordial physics. We investigate the observational consequences of toroidal compactification and analyze their impact on the primordial power spectrum of the CMB provided by the Planck satellite. Within the current experimental and theoretical uncertainties, we identify a possible indication closely related to spatial-parity breaking, consistent with the presence of six spatial extra dimensions in the early Universe, compactified at the GUT epoch before the start of inflation. Finally, we extend our framework to B-mode polarization, highlighting its potential as a sensitive probe in forthcoming ground-based and space-borne experiments with unprecedented precision.

hep-th.title: Higher-Rank Connections and Deformed Schrödinger Operators
hep-th.author: Jonah Baerman, Alba Grassi, Giovanni Ravazzini
hep-th.abstract: We study the connection problem for a class of linear differential equations of order $N$ closely related to the Baxter equation of the quantum Toda chain. The space of solutions is $N$-dimensional and several linearly independent solutions decay at each singularity, leading to a rich structure of boundary value problems. We derive the weakest quantization conditions compatible with decaying behavior at both singularities, and formulate these conditions in terms of the associated monodromy data. In doing so, we prove the quantization conditions predicted by the topological string/spectral theory duality for a family of deformed Schrödinger equations. More generally, our results point to a hierarchy of spectral problems interpolating between the minimal conditions studied here and the maximally decaying boundary conditions of the $N$-particle quantum Toda chain.

hep-th.title: Constraints on regular black holes with nonminimally coupled electromagnetic fields
hep-th.author: Ana Bokulić, Tajron Jurić, Luka Kanai Pejić, Filip Požar, Ivica Smolić
hep-th.abstract: Construction of physically realistic theories admitting regular black hole solutions remains an important open problem in gravitational physics. While theories with electromagnetic fields minimally coupled to gravity have been extensively studied over the past two decades, theories with nonminimal couplings remain comparatively unexplored. We investigate theories containing the interaction terms $R F_{ab}F^{ab}$, $R_{ab} F^a_{\ \, c} \, F^{bc}$ and $R_{abcd} F^{ab} F^{cd}$, which generically arise in low-energy effective Lagrangians. We prove that magnetically charged regular black holes are excluded, except possibly for a special choice of coupling constants, and argue that a similar conclusion applies to electrically charged regular black holes. We further show that similar conclusions hold for Lagrangian terms of the form $f(R,F_{ab}{\star F}^{ab})$.

hep-th.title: Fragility of stealth solutions in mimetic gravity
hep-th.author: Alireza Allahyari, Clarisse Donio, Mohammad Ali Gorji, Reera Gorji, Javad T. Firouzjaee
hep-th.abstract: We study a broad class of constrained mimetic-type extensions of general relativity with action $S=\int{\rm d}^4x\sqrt{-g}\,\bigl(R/2+\lambda\,C[g,\Psi]+{\cal L}_{\rm m}\bigr)$, where $R$ is the Ricci scalar, $\lambda$ is a Lagrange multiplier, $C[g,\Psi]$ is a scalar functional of the metric and generic field content $\Psi$ (possibly involving $\Psi$ and its covariant derivatives) and ${\cal L}_{\rm m}$ is the matter Lagrangian. On the branch $\bar{\lambda}=0$, with the bar denoting a background value, the constrained sector drops out of the background dynamics, so, on domains where a background profile $\bar\Psi$ satisfying $\bar C=0$ exists, the theory admits the corresponding general relativity geometries as stealth solutions. As an explicit illustration, we consider the scalar field case, where $C=g^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\phi\partial_\nu\phi\pm1=0$ becomes a Hamilton-Jacobi equation selecting geodesic congruences. In this setting, we discuss spherically symmetric and rotating stealth profiles using Carter separability. We then analyze perturbations at the general level. The quadratic terms weighted by $\bar\lambda$ vanish on the stealth branch, while the nonlinear constraint still holds order by order and nonlinear interactions need not vanish. Consequently, reproducing GR at the background level does not ensure a uniform $\bar\lambda\to0$ limit for perturbations, and strong coupling may arise.

hep-th.title: The Status of Single Scalar Field Dark Energy
hep-th.author: Carlos García-García, Pedro G. Ferreira, William J. Wolf
hep-th.abstract: We present an assessment of the current observational status of single scalar field models of dark energy. Motivated by recent cosmological measurements -- including baryon acoustic oscillations, Type Ia supernovae, and CMB data -- we examine whether a dynamical scalar field offers a viable explanation for the accelerated expansion of the Universe. Working within an effective field theory (EFT) framework, we argue that cosmological observations are fundamentally limited and can at most constrain a small number of parameters that govern scalar field dynamics. We show that quintessence remains only marginally distinguishable from a cosmological constant, $\Lambda$, and that more general EFT extensions exhibit modest statistical preference, though such evidence is sensitive to data set selection and prior assumptions. These extended models generically predict fifth forces and modifications to the growth of structure, raising challenges from astrophysical constraints. We compare their predictions with current growth rate measurements, Integrated Sachs-Wolfe (ISW) effect and Solar System constraints. We emphasize that viable screening mechanisms remain theoretically non-trivial and observationally testable. On the other hand, we find that current ISW and growth data remain largely in agreement. Looking ahead to Stage IV surveys we forecast improvements in constraints on the dark energy behaviour; although there will be some tightening of bounds, we argue that the problem of underdetermination will persist. We conclude that while single scalar field dark energy remains a natural and flexible framework, its ultimate viability will hinge on improved low-redshift growth measurements and a clearer understanding of gravitational screening.

hep-th.title: Symmetry-based resolution of pseudogauge ambiguities in local equilibrium
hep-th.author: Carlos Hoyos
hep-th.abstract: The total angular momentum current can be decomposed into orbital and spin contributions in different ways, known as pseudogauges. This freedom leads to ambiguities in the definition of local-equilibrium density operators, which in turn affect estimates of spin polarization in heavy-ion collisions. In this work, the pseudogauge ambiguity, together with other ambiguities associated with improvements of conserved currents, is reformulated in terms of spurious symmetries corresponding to conserved currents with vanishing total charge. A prescription for the unambiguous definition of a local-equilibrium density operator, defined as deviating from global equilibrium only by small gradients, is introduced using the currents associated with genuine symmetries. The resulting density operator is invariant under transformations that add improvement terms to local currents, including the energy-momentum tensor.

hep-th.title: Searching for symmetric mass generation with staggered fermions in four dimensions
hep-th.author: Nouman Butt, Simon Catterall, Gwen Hartshaw, Anna Hasenfratz
hep-th.abstract: We conduct numerical simulations to map out the phase diagram and critical behavior of a lattice Higgs model composed of two massless staggered fermion fields forming a doublet under a global $SU(2)$ and coupled to a scalar field in the adjoint representation of the group. The scalar action consists of a potential comprising quadratic and quartic terms and a scalar kinetic term. At fixed quartic coupling we explore a two-dimensional parameter space finding a massless symmetric phase at weak coupling and a massive symmetric phase (SMG phase) at strong coupling. An intermediate anti-ferromagnetic phase separates these two regimes. These results are consistent with leading order weak and strong coupling expansions. We find that the critical lines bounding the intermediate phase merge at a unique point where all fermion bilinear condensates vanish but fermion susceptibilities diverge as non-trivial powers of the lattice size. We conjecture that this merged point corresponds to a multicritical point and may describe a phase consisting of a condensate of certain topological defects.

hep-th.title: Stationary Rotating Geometries Associated with Nonsingular Pulsating Collapse
hep-th.author: A. D. Souza, F. A. Brito, J. Spinelly
hep-th.abstract: Since the first exact solutions of General Relativity (GR) were obtained, it became clear that the theory predicts a new class of compact objects: black holes. The Hawking--Penrose singularity theorems show that, under appropriate assumptions, gravitational collapse in GR leads to singular behavior. Motivated by the expectation that such regimes require physics beyond classical GR, effective approaches inspired by Loop Quantum Cosmology (LQC) and braneworld scenarios introduce high-density corrections. In this work we consider the static exterior geometry introduced by Gao, Lu, Shen, and Faraoni, associated with a comoving interior model in which the singularity is avoided through a sequence of collapse and bounce phases. Using the Newman--Janis algorithm in the Azreg-Aïnou formulation, we construct a stationary rotating exterior extension of this geometry. The resulting line element describes a stationary axisymmetric rotating spacetime whose horizon geometry, angular velocity, surface gravity, and Hawking temperature recover the Kerr and Schwarzschild limits when the quantum/braneworld correction becomes negligible ($l\to 0$). We further analyze the thermal response at fixed rotational state-space parameter, identify Davies-type singular points, and formulate an extended thermodynamic state-space relation.

hep-th.title: Chern bounds and tangent geometry of polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds
hep-th.author: Atsushi Kanazawa
hep-th.abstract: We study the numerical geography and tangent geometry of very amply polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds $(X,H)$ through the positivity of the first jet bundle $J^1(H)$. Let $d=\int_X H^3$, $c=\int_Xc_2(X) H$, and $e=\int_X c_3(X)$. We obtain $e\ge-5d-c-c^2/(4d)$ by mixed intersections on $\mathbb{P}(J^1(H)^*)$, and $e\ge40d\left[(1-\frac{c}{10d})^{3/2}-1\right]$ by a volume estimate for a perturbed tautological class. In particular, the latter inequality shows $e+6c\ge0$, improving Sun's inequality $e+10c\ge0$. As consequences, we show (1) the uniform Hodge bounds $-4d-80\le h^{1,1}(X)-h^{2,1}(X)\le173d/66$, (2) the lower bound $\mathrm{deg} X^\vee\ge78$ for the dual hypersurface, and (3) the upper bound $d\le34$ in the critical case $X\subset\mathbb{P}^6$.

hep-th.title: Charged Klein--Gordon modes on an Ellis wormhole: magnetic confinement and conditional Heun-polynomial solvability
hep-th.author: Abdullah Guvendi, Omar Mustafa
hep-th.abstract: We study a charged Klein--Gordon field on the complete $(2+1)$-dimensional Ellis wormhole, coupled to the pullback of a uniform ambient magnetic field. The induced gauge potential is regular, whereas the intrinsic magnetic pseudoscalar reverses sign across the throat. For $\alpha_B>0$, the radial operator is unitarily equivalent to a self-adjoint one-dimensional Schrödinger operator with a smooth confining potential and discrete spectrum. The radial equation is reduced to confluent-Heun form, and polynomial solvability is shown to require two independent termination conditions. These conditions yield degree-zero Gaussian modes, degree-one states of both global parities, and representative degree-two even states. Exact Ellis-measure normalization is obtained for the degree-zero and degree-one modes. An independent fourth-order full-line finite-difference calculation validates the analytic benchmarks and determines the first eight eigenvalues and their parities. In the double-well regime, the forbidden-region action determines the leading semiclassical exponential of the even--odd level splitting.

hep-th.title: Unified spatiotemporal quantum states and spatiotemporal entanglement from Kirkwood-Dirac phase space
hep-th.author: Zhian Jia, Mei-Hui Xiao
hep-th.abstract: The notion of a spatiotemporal quantum state extends the conventional concept of a spatial quantum state to the spatiotemporal domain. Such states are represented by unit-trace operators that encode correlations among quantum events distributed across space and time. In this work, we use the spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac phase space to provide a unified characterization of spatiotemporal quantum states. Spatiotemporal states obtained from Kirkwood-Dirac distributions are generally non-Hermitian and nonnormal; whereas those constructed from Margenau-Hill distributions are Hermitian. We provide a unification via (quasi)probabilistic mixture of Kirkwwod-Dirac spatiotemporal states which encompasses almost all existing formulations of spatiotemporal quantum states. We derive recursive expressions for spatiotemporal states and elucidate the relation between Kirkwood-Dirac nonclassicality and the temporality of spatiotemporal states. We further extend the construction to many-fold correlation functions and establish its connection with out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs). We also develop a more general unifying framework based on (quasi)probabilistic mixture of $s$-parametrized spatiotemporal states and establish their Petz time reversal and application in studying Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) condition in two-time setting. Finally, we apply this framework to characterize quantum entanglement in spacetime and analyze spatiotemporal entanglement using several complementary entropy measures.

hep-th.title: Black Holes and Scalar Propagation in Three-Dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet Gravity
hep-th.author: Cendikiawan Suryaatmadja
hep-th.abstract: We derive an analytic black-hole family in three-dimensional scalar--tensor Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity with positive coupling. A single implicit equation determines the static circular metric and a scalar linear in time. We show that these solutions exhaust regular nonextremal exteriors with the stated AdS boundary conditions and a fixed nonzero coefficient of time in the scalar. The coupled metric and scalar perturbations have one propagating degree of freedom. On one branch, its kinetic coefficient is positive, its equation is hyperbolic throughout the exterior, and its bulk spatial energy is positive for perturbations of compact support. Scalar signals can cross the metric horizon outward, so exterior evolution needs information from the interior. For linear perturbations with the original metric and scalar boundary values fixed, nonzero compact initial master displacements with zero velocity can evolve only until their first contact with the AdS boundary. We derive this restriction from the original metric and scalar equations.

hep-th.title: Chiral Extensions of Cotangent Yangian
hep-th.author: Keyou Zeng
hep-th.abstract: We construct chiral extensions of the cotangent Yangian using vertex algebroids. At zero level, the construction yields a vertex algebra with a compatible coproduct, whose Zhu reduction recovers the cotangent Yangian of Abedin and Niu. We also construct vertex algebra extensions at non-zero levels and study level-additive coproducts. The zero-level vertex algebra admits two natural quasi-conformal structures. We compute the corresponding sphere one-point conformal blocks and equip each block space with an associative product induced by the coproduct. For the first quasi-conformal structure, the blocks space can be identified with the dual of a certain Lie algebroid homology; for the second, we describe the block algebra and its classical limit in terms of mini-twistor geometry.

hep-th.title: Analytic parity-violating greybody factors of a dynamical Chern-Simons black hole
hep-th.author: Abhishek Rout(University of South Carolina)
hep-th.abstract: We study the low-frequency scattering of gravitational and pseudoscalar waves off a non-rotating black hole in dynamical Chern-Simons (dCS) gravity, where the axial (odd-parity) gravitational sector is irreducibly coupled to the dynamical pseudoscalar while the polar sector remains general relativistic. Working to first order in the dimensionless coupling zeta = (l_CS/M)^4 and using matched asymptotic expansions, we obtain, for the quadrupole (l=2) channel, an exact closed form for the graviton-to-pseudoscalar conversion probability and a high-precision analytic reconstruction of the absorption (greybody) asymmetry. Both reduce to combinations of pi^4, pi^2, and rational numbers, with no ln2 or odd-zeta terms in the reconstructed basis; the transmission-phase sector, by contrast, is governed by an analytically derived static integral involving Apery's constant zeta(3), with its matching prefactor identified numerically. The parity-violating reflection-phase asymmetry is strongly suppressed at low frequency -- well below the parity-even general-relativistic reflection phase -- so that any polarization rotation imprinted on the reflected wave is negligible, while a subleading O(omega*zeta) asymmetry remains in the transmitted phase. These effects are intrinsically strong-field and low-frequency: the normalized flux asymmetries are consistent with a 1/(M*omega)^2 falloff in the geometric-optics limit, where the leading remaining flux effect is conversion loss. The matched-asymptotic results are checked against direct two-channel integration, and the integral determining the absorption asymmetry is evaluated to high precision within an analytically controlled transcendental basis. The coefficients provide analytic targets linking dCS parity violation in absorption and mode conversion to the axial/polar quasinormal-mode splitting.

hep-th.title: Towards ultrarelativistic scattering near the light ring: asymptotic divergence of gravitational-wave fluxes
hep-th.author: David Trestini, Riccardo Gonzo, Benjamin Leather
hep-th.abstract: Near the threshold between scattering and capture by a Schwarzschild black hole, a particle spends a long time close to an unstable circular orbit, which in the ultrarelativistic limit approaches the light ring. Here we study the behavior of the gravitational wave fluxes emitted by such an ultrarelativistic particle at first order in the mass ratio. The fluxes radiated to infinity and absorbed by the horizon diverge as the inverse distance from the light ring multiplied by its logarithm. Using the Wentzel, Kramers, and Brillouin (WKB) approximation to solve the Regge-Wheeler equation and treating the infinite harmonic sum analytically, we derive an exact expression for the coefficient of this logarithmic enhancement and show that it is identical for both fluxes.
